title: Portrait of a Romanian-American Missionary Priest: Anniversary at Holy Trinity Parish, Rochester / Victor, NY
intro:
“Zeal for Your house has eaten me up” Psalms: 68.11 

 

On Sunday, October 10, 2022, His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae took part in the festivities marking the 20th anniversary of the priestly ordination of Fr. Daniel Ene, Eparchial Secretary of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, Dean of New York, New England and the Eastern US, and parish priest of Holy Trinity Church in Rochester/Victor, NY. The celebration was doubled by the parish’s own 20th anniversary, since it was founded in the same year, 2002.

Fr. Daniel Ene graduated from the Theological Seminary and the Faculty of Theology in Bucharest and for several years was a supervisor, secretary and teacher at the Theological Seminary in Bucharest. In 2002, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae ordained him deacon and then priest for Holy Trinity Parish in Rochester, NY; he was the first parish priest of this parish and the first deacon and priest ordained by His Eminence after his consecration as a hierarch in July 2002.

Over his 20 years of ministry, Fr. Daniel has held several administrative positions within the Archdiocese/Metropolia. From 2008 he served as eparchial secretary,  and then as dean. Fr. Daniel is also the president of the Metropolia’s Education Commission and coordinator of the Romanian Orthodox Ladies’ Auxiliary (AROLA). More recently, by the charge of His Eminence Nicolae, Fr. Daniel also cares for the Romanian communities in Latin America.

On this occasion, His Eminence celebrated the Divine Liturgy together with an assembly of priests made up of Rev. Fr. Nicholas Apostola, Administrative Vicar of the Metropolia, Rev. Fr. Grigorie Țăpuc of St. Matthew the Apostle Parish in Ottawa, Canada, and Rev. Fr. Ștefan Drăgoi of Saints Joachim and Anna Parish in Seattle, WA, together with the parish priest, Fr. Daniel Ene. The special guest was Archdeacon Prof. Sorin Mihalache. In his homily, the Metropolitan stressed the importance of catechizing young people in order to protect them from spiritual death and bring them before Christ. At the end of the service, His Eminence addressed a word in English to the English-speaking faithful, speaking to them about the Holy Brâncoveanu Martyrs, whose Holy Relics he had brought for veneration on this occasion.

At the end of the service, as a sign of esteem and appreciation, Fr. Daniel received from His Eminence a Holy pectoral Cross, as Fr. Daniel already holds all the distinctions the Patriarchate/Metropolia can offer. From the priests serving in the Eastern Deanery he received a portable liturgical kit to use at missionary services in Latin America, and from some of the faithful he received a vestment embroidered in the traditional style of the Maramureș region. In turn, Rev. Fr. Daniel Ene offered His Eminence a silver icon of the Mother of God and gave gifts to the priests present.

As a sign of high appreciation for the work of this tireless servant of the Church, Their Excellencies the ambassadors of the countries where Fr. Daniel has made missionary visits, as well as the leaders of the Romanian communities in those countries, sent messages of congratulations and gratitude for the pastoral care he has shown over the years.

The Divine Liturgy was followed by a festive banquet, during which representatives of the Romanian communities of central and western New York State delivered messages of appreciation, and the messages received from Latin America were read.

Axios!

 

Reported by

Fr. Ștefan Drăgoi, participant

 

Below we present some paragraphs from the messages received from the Romanian Embassies in the countries of Latin America and from representatives of the Romanian communities:

 

BRAZIL          

“Our good thoughts turn today, on this festive day, to you, Fr. Daniel. Completing 20 years of ministry and of preaching the word of God is no small thing. We thank you for being there, and we thank God for making possible our meeting here in São Paulo. We are Romanians cast by fate into such a hostile world; we live with longing for home and for our parents, for our traditions and for God. Your presence among us has restored our faith and brought hope and blessing into our homes. Your coming to São Paulo in November 2021 (after the long and trying period of the pandemic) was a ray of light for us. We know all too well what travel conditions were like at that time, but that did not stop you from facing the difficulties and reaching the “lost sheep” in São Paulo (Brazil) and in other Romanian communities in South America.

You are an example of humility, vocation and spiritual grace. May God give you health and strength to continue this work, so beautiful and so essential in the times we live in. We felt your love for people from the very first moment we met you, when you won us over with your naturalness and your humor. We await you with love anytime, and even though we are few in number, we assure you of all our love and respect. With much love, the Petruțiu family: Natalia, Felicia and Adrian.” Mr. Adrian Petruțiu, São Paulo Philharmonic, member of the Romanian community

 

BOLIVIA

“On the occasion of the 20th anniversary of the priestly ordination of the Very Reverend Father DANIEL ADRIAN ENE and the 20th anniversary of the founding of “Holy Trinity” Parish in Rochester, New York, of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, the Honorary Consulate General of Romania in the Plurinational State of Bolivia has the honor of conveying its most sincere and warm congratulations to Fr. Daniel for his 20 years of pastoral and missionary work and for his contribution to preserving the Orthodox faith abroad, together with wishes for health, strength and spiritual inspiration in this holy mission entrusted to him. The Romanian community in La Paz, Bolivia, rejoiced greatly in the presence of Fr. Daniel, and we can say it was a historic moment, because for the first time we heard a Te Deum and a Memorial Service in the Romanian language, an event also attended by the Greek and Cypriot community of La Paz. It was also a moving moment to hear Romanian words and the “Our Father” prayer among the high peaks of the Andes. We are convinced that these 20 years in the service of God represent the dedication and love of Fr. Daniel, who through his spiritual work is close to the Romanian soul, maintaining the priestly bond with the Romanian communities of South America. We are deeply grateful to Fr. Daniel Ene for his care: despite suffering the effects of the lack of oxygen and altitude sickness (the city of La Paz lies at an altitude of 4,100 meters), Fr. Daniel insisted on continuing the Christian service. We reiterate our congratulations and wish him a long ministry, peace and much divine grace in his holy mission, and may the good God bless his life and his family.” Mrs. Tereza Șelaru, Honorary Consul  General of Romania in Bolivia.

 

CHILE

“On the 20th anniversary of your ordination, I wish you much health, peace and patience to continue the beautiful task the good God has entrusted to you: to shepherd the community in North America, and us as well, those in the South. May the good God give you strength and light your path so that you can work to increase the number of Orthodox faithful in the diaspora.  Many years! With much love, Ioana Galea” Representative of the Romanian community in Santiago de Chile, Chile

 

COLOMBIA

“…Very beloved Father Daniel, dear brother, friend and companion in struggle and apostolic and missionary work, these are twenty years of service and ministerial life, of excellent service to the people of God and to his Church, the one that in Colombia and Venezuela through his love, humility, simplicity and dedication without half was able to verify that to love God is to love our fellow men, especially the poorest and humblest….” His Grace Bishop Timoteo of Assos, Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Columbia and Venezuela

 

“Allow me to wish you a warm “Many years!”, knowing that we are in your prayers, just as you are in our thoughts and hearts as a guardian of the faith, caring for all of us Romanians scattered throughout this Western Hemisphere, from North to South. Both in Venezuela, at the beautiful wooden church in the Maramureș style, and in Bogotá, Colombia, where through his zeal a Divine Liturgy was celebrated in Romanian for the first time in 2021, as well as at the many stops across Latin America, Fr. Daniel’s work is extremely important when seen in perspective. Equally impressive are his mission, zeal and determination, for in all this journeying across Central and South America to comfort the hearts of the Romanians scattered throughout these lands, one does not see the long hours on planes and in airports, the sleepless nights, the last efforts to the point of exhaustion, the attempts to save, for example, a young Romanian gone astray in Cali and set him on a path.” Her Excellency Mrs. Claudia Tuşa, Chargé d’Affaires a.i.  Head of Mission of Romania in Colombia

 

ECUADOR

“On the 20th anniversary of the blessed day on which you were ordained and began your most beneficial work as priest of the parish in Rochester, we wish to recall with gratitude the effort you have made to reach even the more remote corners of the world, such as Ecuador, and to bring us the joy of the Divine Liturgy and the Holy Sacraments of our Lord Jesus Christ. Your concern for the Romanian Orthodox Christian faithful of South America has given you the strength to overcome distances and cultural, social and geographical differences, and to make your way to places where the need for Orthodox services is a painful reality. We thank you for this and hope to continue to enjoy your care! On this date of the utmost importance both for you and for the faithful you shepherd, we send you our congratulations and our good wishes! Many years ahead in health and spiritual profit! May God help! Respectfully, Mădălina Chirilă, Quito-Ecuador” Mrs. Mădălina Chirilă - representative of the Romanian Community in Quito, Ecuador 

 

MEXICO

“I have known Fr. Daniel from the very beginning of my mandate in Mexico. Of course his reputation preceded him; of course my good colleagues, Romanian and Mexican alike, anticipated our meeting with the warm words with which they described him. More than that, before I saw him, I came across traces of Father’s devout passage at every step through the embassy: icons, prayer books and pious signs already marked the territory of the Mission and formed, together with Father’s luminous image, an unmistakable whole of Orthodox faith. Then I met him. Impossible to overlook, calm and feverish at the same time, always on the run yet never in a hurry when face to face, a jovial man yet deeply serious, cheerful and dramatic within the same instant, Fr. Daniel moved me for good, above all through his thirst for service. I never caught him resting, never content that the toil was over and that he could catch his breath for a moment, always torn between the sacrifice just offered and the service to come. Father is loved and awaited in Mexico. I saw this both in the capital and in Cancún. The “Mexican” Romanians, whom Father always carries in his prayers anyway, would like to have him more often than Vladyka Nicolae or the long-suffering Presvytera Flavia might allow. The “Mexican” Romanians do not realize it, but Father’s energy and zeal are still more than they could bear. And for this reason, Father’s bold plans in Mexico have not yet been fulfilled… Glory to God for all things! Marius Gabriel Lazurca, Ambassador of Romania to Mexico and Central America”  His Excellency Mr. Marius-Gabriel LAZURCA, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Romania to the United Mexican States

 

“…Almost 4 years ago, one afternoon, I searched Google for an email address of the Metropolia or a contact in the United States, and I found the email of Fr. Daniel Ene. I sent him an email hoping he would answer, because I felt the spiritual need for a priest in Cancún, Mexico, where I lived. There are several hundred Romanians here, and we had long hoped to have a church… Through enormous personal effort, Father managed to ease our homesickness a little by celebrating services at the Church of St. Mary Undoer of Knots… God’s ways are mysterious, but one thing is very certain, as a book by Holy Father Arsenie Boca says: Fost-a om trimis de Dumnezeu. Fr. Ene was sent by God to ease our longing, to remind us of the order of the soul and to accompany us like a true shepherd who cares for our souls lost throughout the world… We are grateful for everything he does for us, for the services he celebrates here, for the dedication and humility with which he carries them out, and above all for the faith he has in God. From here in Cancún we wish him much health and many years of life, and may the good God grant that he visit us for many years to come. With esteem and great respect, Eugen Degeratu” Mr. Eugen Degeratu, Representative of the Romanian Community in Cancún, Mexico.

 

PERU

“…First of all, I would like to congratulate you on completing 20 years of spiritual work in the service of the Romanian communities on the American continent, and especially for the care you have shown our Romanians in the Latin American countries. Thank you for your tireless effort to come to Latin America, to Peru, Ecuador and Bolivia, to bring comfort to the souls of the Romanians in these faraway countries and to give them advice and a helping hand when they need it. I know it is not easy for you to make these journeys, and that is why we all appreciate the strength and dedication with which you come each time to let prayers and the Romanian language be heard in the churches that always welcome us with joy. Even in difficult conditions such as those in Bolivia, you fulfilled your duty toward the Romanians of La Paz and left a beautiful memory, as a sign of the sacrifice you make with an open heart. I wish you much health and strength, may you have as many faithful as possible at your side, and may you strengthen them through the power of the holy word and of prayer!  Ambassador Camelia Ion-Radu PERU” Her Excellency Mrs. Camelia Ion-Radu, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Romania to the Republic of PERU

“I wish to send a greeting of congratulations to Fr. Daniel Ene on the 20th anniversary of his ordination to the priesthood and his installation as parish priest. I had the joy of meeting Fr. Daniel Ene on his first visit to Lima, in December 2017. For us, members of the Romanian community in Peru, this first visit was an enormous surprise; it was moving to hear the Divine Liturgy in Romanian and to feel the presence of a representative of the Romanian Orthodox Church in our midst. Fr. Ene returned to Lima toward the end of the pandemic, in November 2021, and again in 2022, and these visits are clear proof that our ancestral Church stands by us in an increasingly globalized world, and also in a world convulsed by the pandemic and condemned to periods of isolation. Fr. Daniel Ene is a pioneer of itinerant pastoral care in South America, his visits over the last 5 years covering a large part of Latin America: Peru, Chile, Ecuador, Colombia, Mexico, Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay. He carries the banner of Romanian Orthodoxy into areas where the Romanian communities are not very numerous, which gives added importance to the message we perceive, that the Church is close to us.

The Church has always been a point of reference in the lives of us Romanians, wherever we are in the world. We are happy to be able to have Orthodox religious life in Lima and to promote Romanian spirituality, and Fr. Daniel Ene’s exhortations help us keep our faith alive and preserve our Orthodox traditions and our cohesion as members of the Romanian community. On this anniversary, I wish to send you congratulations for all the work you have done over the past 20 years, and our thoughts of thanks and gratitude for your dedicated ministry and for the tireless effort you have made to carry out the pastoral-missionary and cultural task you pursue with rich fruit. Many happy and healthy years, Father! Ioana Ciaușu - Ioana Ciaușu, Member of the Romanian community in Peru 

 

VENEZUELA

“El nombre de la comunidad ortodoxa rumana de Venezuela y la iglesia San Constantino y Santa Elena queremos expresar nuestra felicitación a nuestro querido hermano en el Ministerio padre Daniel n por su aniversario número 20 de ordenación sacerdotal El señor Dios Todopoderoso quién nos da la alegría de la vida y de llevar este ministerio compás le conceda larga vida y mucho entusiasmo por todas las cosas maravillosas que faltan por hacer Dios nos bendiga 1000 felicidades padre Daniel les deseamos todos los hermanos desde Venezuela” Fr. Geraldo Antonio Garcia, Parish Priest of SS. Constantine and Helen Church, Caracas, Venezuela.

 

“As president of the Parish Council of SS. Constantine and Helen Romanian Orthodox Church, I have had several telephone conversations with Fr. Daniel in his capacity as secretary of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, headquartered in Chicago, as well as two occasions of personal contact during his trips to Caracas in 2021 and 2022. Thanks to the attention he has given our church and the support he has given us, especially since 2019, we have received a quarterly financial contribution that has been crucial for the functioning of our church. As I said at the beginning, I had the opportunity to meet him twice. The first meeting was in August 2021, when, in the midst of the pandemic, he organized a visit to Caracas together with two consuls from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, whose visit was made possible by Father’s timely intervention with the Ministry’s authorities. This itinerant consulate was needed to resolve consular matters for Romanian citizens, since the Romanian Embassy had been closed since 2019. ……

In May of this year we again received Fr. Daniel, who celebrated the Liturgy on the feast of Saints Constantine and Helen, May 21, 2022, and on the following day presided, together with Fr. Antonio, parish priest of our church, over the Extraordinary General Assembly of the parishioners. We thank Fr. Daniel for giving us invaluable support in the repair of our church. Soon our church will have a renovated roof that will last another 25 years. Please accept our recognition and congratulations on the 20th anniversary of your priesthood. Respectfully, Denu Niculescu” Mr. Denu Niculescu, President of the Parish Council of SS. Constantine and Helen Church in Caracas, Venezuela

title: Historic Pilgrimage to Romanian Orthodox Communities in the USA
intro:
With the blessing of His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel, at the invitation of His Eminence Nicolae, Romanian Orthodox Metropolitan of the Americas, from September 26 to October 12, the reliquary with the right hand of Saint Nicholas the Hierarch and fragments of the relics of the Holy Martyr Prince Constantin Brâncoveanu were carried to several Romanian communities across the Ocean

The relics of Saint Constantin Brâncoveanu were given by the Patriarch of Romania to two Romanian Orthodox Christian communities: the “Holy Brâncoveanu Martyrs” Mission in Fairfield, Connecticut, shepherded by parish priest Fr. Mihai Faur, and “Resurrection of the Lord” Church in San Francisco, where Fr. Octavian Mahler is the parish priest. This shows that His Beatitude wishes to make known in the diaspora the Romanians’ devotion to these great martyrs of our Romanian nation and of our Romanian Orthodox Church. That is precisely why the joy was complete. 

 

A Moving and Beautiful Welcome in Chicago

The spiritual itinerary was a great spiritual joy for the Romanian Orthodox clergy and faithful in the United States of America. It is no coincidence that Patriarch Daniel blessed this pilgrimage in the year marking two decades since the episcopal ordination of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae. That is precisely why our first stop was at the “Holy Emperors Constantine and Helen” Metropolitan Cathedral in Chicago, where the hierarch personally received the holy treasures on the evening of Monday, September 26, the day of commemoration of Saint Prince Neagoe Basarab.

On Tuesday, September 27, the Divine Liturgy on the feast day of the Holy Hieromartyr Anthimos the Iberian, Metropolitan of Wallachia, was celebrated by a group of clergy led by His Eminence Nicolae. Although these were working days during the week, Monday and Tuesday, the faithful came in large numbers to the Holy and Divine Liturgy, as well as to the Akathist services in the evening. Here we thanked Metropolitan Nicolae and the Romanian community for the warm and joyful welcome they gave the delegation carrying the holy treasures. 

 

Venerating the Relics of Saint John Maximovitch

From Chicago we flew to San Francisco. On the way from the airport to where we were staying, our host, Fr. Octavian Mahler, parish priest of the “Resurrection of the Lord and the Holy Icon of the Mother of God of Hawaii” Church, suggested a brief stop for reflection at the church where the incorrupt relics of Saint John Maximovitch of San Francisco rest. It was a deeply moving encounter. I cannot describe in words what we experienced here when, for a few minutes, the hand of Saint Nicholas the Hierarch of Myra in Lycia was placed above the reliquary of another holy hierarch who, by the will of the Lord, worked many miracles. Everything was transformed into light.

In San Francisco we found a beautiful community of Orthodox Romanians who impressed me. From there we set out on a spiritual marathon that stretched over nearly 10,000 kilometers in three American states: Illinois, California and Washington. Our host, together with Fr. Octavian Mahler, was Dr. Felicia Radu Rădulescu. We take this opportunity to thank them both for their hospitality and for the efforts they made to support our travels so that we would reach each community safely and on time. Every day we had a schedule planned to the minute in order to include all the communities that had requested our presence, keeping in mind that the distances were very great. On the feast of the Protection of the Mother of God, Saturday, October 1, we celebrated the Divine Liturgy at “Holy Cross” Church in San Jose, California, shepherded by parish priest Fr. Constantin Lăpuștea and concelebrating priest Fr. Florin Lăpuștea, in a moving atmosphere and in a spirit of joy and Romanian and Orthodox brotherhood. The next day, Sunday, October 2, we served at “Resurrection of the Lord” Church in Sacramento, California, together with parish priest Fr. Alin Galoanță, in an extremely welcoming Orthodox community.  

From Monday, October 3, to Wednesday, October 5, we were in Seattle, Washington State, as guests of the community led by parish priest Fr. Ștefan Drăgoi. After a beautiful welcome at Saints Joachim and Anna Church in Seattle, with a group of priests of various nationalities from several churches in Washington State, the relics were placed for veneration in front of the Holy Altar, where they remained all day until late in the evening, since Christians came from the whole metropolitan area, some even from Vancouver, Canada. For nine hours rivers of people flowed to venerate the hand of Saint Nicholas the Hierarch and the relics of the Holy Martyr Constantin Brâncoveanu.

A heartfelt gathering followed at the “Elevation of the Holy Cross” Parish in Upland, Los Angeles. We take this opportunity to thank the good Archimandrite Nicodim Bibarţ, as well as the Orthodox faithful, Romanian and of other nationalities, for the moving welcome.

Everywhere we met people who were happy for this blessing granted by His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel and His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae. The Romanians, clergy and faithful alike, unanimously expressed their thanks for this historic visit to America. Among them were elderly or sick people who could never have traveled to Romania to venerate these holy treasures. Many communities that would have liked to receive us remained unvisited, since they were not included in the program. 

 

The Relics of Saint Constantin Brâncoveanu for the Romanians of San Francisco

On Saturday, October 8, we returned with the holy treasures to Sacramento, this time to the “Holy Archangels Michael and Gabriel” Parish, where Fr. Rareș Onofrei is the parish priest. After the official welcome of the delegation, we took part in the liturgical program, followed by a homily, in the presence of clergy and faithful who were Romanian, American and of other nationalities.

In the afternoon we returned to San Francisco. On Sunday, October 9, we took part in the autumn patronal feast of the “Resurrection of the Lord and the Icon of the Mother of God of Hawaii” Church. A rich liturgical program took place here, arranged by parish priest Fr. Octavian Mahler. At the end of the Divine Liturgy I gave the lecture entitled “Christian Martyrdom, the Apotheosis of Man’s Encounter with God” before a large audience. On this occasion, with the blessing of His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel, the Romanian community received a gift of great spiritual value: a reliquary with a fragment of the relics of the Holy Martyr Prince Constantin Brâncoveanu.

At the end of this spiritual marathon on American soil, we lived unique moments in San Francisco. Before we returned to Romania, the myrrh-streaming and wonderworking icon of the Mother of God of Hawaii met the hand of Saint Nicholas, the hierarch who is an image of meekness, the defender of the faith and of the teaching on the veneration of the Mother of God in the Church. We thank once again Deacon Nectarie, who came from Hawaii for such a mystical, holy and blessed encounter. We also thank Fr. Octavian Mahler for facilitating this historic event. A great and beautiful surprise for us was that Fr. Nectarie gave us a copy of the wonderworking Icon of the Mother of God of Hawaii and a few small bottles of the myrrh that flowed from this wondrous treasure. 

I was very impressed to meet many Americans who had converted to Orthodoxy in several parishes. They were in good order, almost the first to receive the holy treasures, which was exceptional. People who truly live their faith, not Orthodox by convenience. Orthodox faithful from the communities of the sister Orthodox Churches also took part: Slavs, Greeks, Antiochians and others, who came because of their devotion to Saint Nicholas the Hierarch, but on this occasion also learned about the life of the Holy Brâncoveanu Martyrs.

Orthodox Christianity, one of the largest websites in its field, reported on this bringing of the hand of Saint Nicholas the Hierarch and the relics of the Holy Martyr Prince Constantin Brâncoveanu on pilgrimage to the United States of America. In this way our Orthodox spirituality becomes known, as well as the fact that this treasure of great price is found in Bucharest, the capital of Romania, and that we Romanians venerate great saints such as the Brâncoveanu Martyrs. They are great for all of Orthodox Christendom.

It was truly a unique and very beautiful experience, and a very great joy that His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel, through his high blessing, granted to the clergy and faithful of the United States of America. 

 

Fr. Dr. Emil Nedelea Cărămizaru 

Text taken from Ziarul Lumina

intro:

title: Church Music Course
intro:
With the blessing of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, the church music course offered by the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas began on Saturday, November 12, 2022. The course is intended for those who wish to learn psaltic church music and to form choral groups that will provide the chanting at the analogion in the parishes of the Metropolia.

The highest calling of a Christian is the praise offered to God, through which he becomes like the heavenly hosts who sing unceasingly around the throne of God. We express this in singing the Cherubic Hymn: “Let us who mystically represent the Cherubim, and who sing the thrice-holy hymn to the life-creating Trinity, now lay aside all earthly cares.”

Organized over two years, the course aims to teach psaltic notation, the typikon for the seven daily services and the Divine Liturgy, and the learning of the tones and their application in the services. The coordinator of this program is Leonard Milea, a protopsaltis well known in our parishes. Leonard Milea is a graduate of the National University of Music in Bucharest, Byzantine music section, and of the Faculty of Orthodox Theology in Bucharest, and a former member of the male choirs Te Deum Laudamus, Armonia and Psalmodia. More than 70 young people and adults from the Metropolia’s parishes in the USA have enrolled in this weekly online course.

With the Lord’s help, and with a desire to learn, perseverance and patience, we hope that this course will fulfill its purpose and that our parishes will enjoy beautiful chanting to the glory of God!

title: Romania’s National Day Celebrated at Guardian Angel Orthodox Day School in the Chicago Area
intro:
Since 2017, at the initiative of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae and with the blessing of the parish priest, Fr. John Rallis, of St. John the Baptist Parish, the administration of Guardian Angel Orthodox Day School has added Romanian to the school’s Foreign Languages program, alongside Greek and Russian. In the 2022-2023 school year, more than 45 children, preschoolers and schoolchildren, are enrolled in the Romanian language program, under the guidance of the Romanian language teachers Preoteasa Sanda Cărbune and Alina Vance.

The celebration of Romania’s National Day, on Wednesday, November 30, 2022, was attended by His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae, Fr. Nicolae Cărbune, Mr. Gheorghe Cârciu, Secretary of State of the Department for Romanians Abroad, Mr. Victor Ionescu of the same department, and Consul Marius Săvuică of the Consulate General of Romania in Chicago. This year, in collaboration with the Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas and GOADS, My Romanian World Publishing House of Chicago printed and distributed free of charge 3,800 books and 100 magazines in Romanian, as part of the project “Promoting the linguistic, cultural and educational identity of Romanian children in the USA,” supported and funded by the Department for Romanians Abroad.

The program of the celebration included patriotic songs, historical skits about Michael the Brave and the traditional dances “Hora Moldovenească,” “Călușarii” and “Hora Unirii.” The children were prepared for the dances by Mrs. Elena Titu of SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago.

The theme of the celebration was thus the symbol of the “hora” in Romanian culture, the unity it expresses and the unity long desired by all speakers of the same tongue, ever since 1600. “The one who gives it deep social meaning and strengthens its historical message is the bard of Mircești, Vasile Alecsandri, through the famous ‘Hora Unirii,’ described by Mihai Eminescu as ‘the most beautiful hora of the Romanian people.’ His verses were set to music by the composer Alexandru Flechtenmacher. From that moment, the hora became the symbol of the brotherhood of all Romanians:

‘Come, let us join hand in hand/ All with a Romanian heart/

Let us dance the hora of brotherhood/ On the land of Romania.’

Since then, for Romania the hora has become a dance and a song, a symbol of victory and of the covenant of those who, as brothers, feel they belong to this people and this land.” (https://hig724.wordpress.com/istoria-horei/)

Alina Vance, Romanian language teacher,

Guardian Angel Orthodox Day School

title: The Armonia Choir Caroled the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas
intro:
On Monday, December 19, 2022, the Armonia Choir of the Archdiocese of Tomis caroled the clergy and faithful of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas. The carol concert took place on the Metropolia’s Facebook platform and was preceded by a word of greeting from His Eminence Archbishop Teodosie of Tomis addressed to His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae on the occasion of his 20 years of mission on the American continent, completed this year. His Eminence Teodosie recalled that His Eminence Nicolae is a son of Dobruja and renewed the invitation to visit his native places at any future opportunity. The members of the Choir performed traditional Romanian carols and carols from the international repertoire.

The Armonia men’s choir was founded in 2001 at the initiative of Archdeacon Assistant Professor Dr. Iulian Dumitru, at the Orthodox Theological Seminary in Tulcea. Since 2004, the Armonia Choir has been under the patronage of the Archdiocese of Tomis, when, together with His Eminence Dr. Teodosie, a new series of religious, classical and folk concerts was launched, held in various cities of Romania.

Between 2006 and 2011, the Armonia choir received numerous invitations abroad. In the summer of 2012, the Armonia choir took part in the international festival “Folklore without Borders” organized in Dobrich, Bulgaria. On the basis of obtaining this award, in the same year the Choir took part in the World Choir Games (Cincinnati, USA), the most prestigious choral competition in the world, where it won two gold medals. The success of this choir did not stop there, however. In July 2013 it took part in the European Choir Games in Graz, Austria, and again won gold in the Folklore category and silver in the Sacred Art category, while in the Male Chamber Choir category it won the Grand Prize. In July 2014 in Riga, Latvia, it took part in the World Choir Games, where it was awarded a gold medal in the Sacred Art category and a gold medal and the Grand Prize in the category Male Chamber Choir. In July 2015 in Magdeburg, Germany, it took part in the European Choir Games & Grand Prix of Nations, where it won a Gold Medal in the category Male Chamber Choir.

Currently, the Armonia Choir is made up of 30 members (clergy, undergraduate and master’s students of the Faculties of Theology and Arts of Ovidius University). Its repertoire is very diverse, consisting of polyphonic and monodic (psaltic) religious pieces, Romanian folk music, traditional Romanian and foreign carols, as well as pieces from the universal classical repertoire (information from https://arhiepiscopiatomisului.ro/corala-ortodoxa-barbateasca-armonia).

title: Christmas at Saint Mary Church in Dacula, Georgia
intro:
Saint Mary Romanian Orthodox Church, dedicated to the Protection of the Mother of God, in Dacula, is a true religious, cultural and social center for Romanians from all over the state of Georgia and the surrounding area. The Nativity of the Lord is usually celebrated in this Romanian-American community with many special activities for everyone. They began with the traditional Romanian craft gathering around the feast of Saint Nicholas, where the young people learned the symbols and kinds of Romanian embroidery and worked on and crafted various projects related to the Romanian heritage, and they culminated in the rich carol concert held on Sunday, December 18, after the Divine Liturgy in the church’s new social hall.

After the Divine Liturgy and a short word from Fr. Nicolae Clempuș, the parish priest, the faithful, young and old, made their way to the new social hall, where everything had been prepared for this special event: the beautifully decorated Christmas tree, the stage set up and the sound system ready.

The concert was opened by the little ones of the children’s choir. More than 40 children sang traditional carols and recited Christmas poems and greetings. The children’s smiles, their cheerfulness and their excitement put us all in that pure spirit of Christmas. After receiving, as a reward for their caroling, a Romanian book, a braided bread and an apple each, the youth choir took the stage.

The active young people of our parish organize many activities related to the Church as well as to the social life of the community. This time they rehearsed carols with Fr. Nicolae Clempuș and presented a special program to the parishioners. Traditional choral carols and performances on piano, violin, guitar, flute, trombone and double bass brought the hall to its feet and impressed the audience. What is even more remarkable is that the young people of Saint Mary’s organized themselves into instrumental groups and learned carols together as duets, quartets and other combinations. The carol Galbenă Gutuie was sung by Fr. Nicolae and Preoteasa Roza-Elena Clempuș, accompanied by guitar, flute and violin.

After the parish youth choir, the members of the Saint Mary Church mixed choir, conducted by Mr. Cristian Gheție, took the stage. The mixed choir performed several traditional carols in four parts: Legănelul lui Iisus, La Betleem colo-n jos, Praznic Luminos and Dacă-n fiecare zi Crăciunul ar sosi.

The 2022 Christmas Concert ended with an instrumental part performed by the children and young people of the parish and a short recital by Alexia Toma and Vivian Panțuru, members of the Atlanta junior philharmonic. Everyone present was served braided breads, apples and gifts.

At the end, all the children gathered around the Christmas tree and received a visit from Santa Claus, who brought gifts for everyone. The most beautiful gift, however, was our offering to the Child Jesus, born in the manger in Bethlehem, and the news of His birth, which we proclaimed to all. The memory remains of a special day at Saint Mary Church in Dacula, Georgia, USA.

Fr. Nicolae Clempuș

title: Thanks for an Act of Christian Fraternity
intro:
His Eminence Nicolae, Romanian Orthodox Metropolitan of the Americas, parish priest Fr.  Gerardo Antonio Gracia and the entire community of Holy Emperors Constantine and Helen Church in Caracas, Venezuela, thank His Grace Iustin, Bishop of Maramureș and Sătmar, and Mother Filoteia, Abbess of Bârsana Monastery, for the donation of the shingles needed to renew the Maramureș-style wooden church in Caracas. The 60,000 shingles offered by the Diocese and the Monastery have arrived in the churchyard and will be installed, after the holy feasts of the Nativity, New Year and Theophany, with the help of Romanian priests and faithful from the USA who are skilled in this work. The cost of shipping was covered by special donations from the Metropolia’s parishes in the USA.

Work on the parish’s new church began in 1994. The initiators of this project were the parish priest, Fr. Costică Popa, who had shepherded the community since its founding in 1968, and attorney Corneliu Popescu, then mayor of the Chacao district, who obtained the land by concession from the El Hatillo city hall. A special contribution was made by Mr. Ionel Sima from Romania, who procured and prepared the timber with the support of the Romanian Commercial Bank and the ARDAF company. The Romanian Patriarchate sent 15 craftsmen led by master builder Gavrilă Hotica, who worked on building the church in 1997-1998. The Romanian Patriarchate also donated the iconostasis, the chandeliers, the icon screen and the stalls, and in April 1998 it sent the family of church painters Sanda and Mihai Horju to carry out the iconography of the church. The consecration of the church was performed on November 7, 1999, by His Beatitude Teoctist, marking the first visit of a Romanian Patriarch to South America, an event with important ecumenical echoes in Venezuela.     

The gesture of Christian fraternity of His Grace Iustin and Mother Abbess Filoteia shows once again the care of the Romanian Orthodox Church, through its worthy servants, for the brothers and sisters far from the Homeland. This project was initiated by Fr. Daniel Ene, diocesan secretary and Dean for the Eastern USA.

On the eve of the holy feasts of the Nativity, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae and the community in Caracas extend wishes of health, peace, joy and spiritual progress to His Grace Iustin, His Grace Timotei Sătmăreanul, Mother Abbess Filoteia and all the priests, faithful and monastics of the Diocese of Maramureș and Sătmar!

Many blessed years!

title: The Feast of the Nativity in Norfolk, VA
intro:
The “Nativity of the Mother of God” Mission in Norfolk, Virginia, celebrated today, December 25,  the Nativity of the Lord, a feast so eagerly awaited by Christians everywhere. After the Divine Liturgy and the reading of the pastoral letter sent by His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae, there followed a program prepared with the children of the Sunday school. The program consisted of a short play depicting the Birth of the Christ Child and a selection of carols proper to this Great Feast of the Lord, sung together with the parish priest, Fr. Orlando Stelian Geonea. 

After the program, the children also enjoyed the gifts they received for the feast. The joy of the Nativity celebration then moved to the social hall,  where a fellowship meal was held and traditional Romanian dishes brought by the parishioners of our parish were served.

May God bless us and grant us all a merry Christmas with health and all good things! 

 

Fr. Orlando Stelian Geonea

title: New Year 2023 at SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago
intro:
At SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago, the New Year 2023 was welcomed with prayer. On Saturday evening, December 31, 2022, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, together with the clergy of the Cathedral, celebrated the Vigil for the Great Feast of the Circumcision of the Lord and of Saint Basil the Great, followed by the Te Deum service before the passing of the year. In his homily at the end of the service, His Eminence Nicolae spoke about the significance of prayer at the beginning of the year:

“In the litanies of the Te Deum service we ask for God’s blessing upon the crown of the year that has begun, for sun, rain and seasonable winds, for health and God’s protection. But we also ask that all heresies and divisions be extinguished, that right faith and piety be planted. We further ask that the Holy Church and all of us be delivered from all affliction, wrath, danger and necessity, and from all enemies visible and invisible. And we also ask that all enmities, disorders and internal strife be quelled. If in the last two years we earnestly asked for health and protection from illness during the pandemic, at this service for the passing into the year 2023 we ask for peace and the quelling of all enmities. We live in a world troubled by war, even between Orthodox brothers, troubled by much division. It is fitting that at this beginning of the Year we should desire peace, reconciliation with God and with our neighbors. The peace of the world can be attained only if each Christian seeks peace of soul. The peace of the world begins with each one of us.”

On New Year’s Day 2023, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, together with the clergy of the Cathedral, celebrated the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great and spoke about the many meanings of the day: the Circumcision of the Lord, a Great Feast; the day dedicated to honoring Saint Basil the Great, Archbishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia; the New Year; and the Sunday before the Baptism of the Lord. He then recalled the tradition of the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church dedicating each year to certain themes. The year 2023 is “the Homage Year of the pastoral care of the elderly” and “the Commemorative Year of hymnographers and church cantors.” Special activities dedicated to the two themes will be organized in the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas. With regard to the second theme, a church music program has already begun for the faithful of the Metropolia’s parishes who wish to become involved in chanting at the cantor’s stand. His Eminence Nicolae concluded by congratulating those who bear the name of Saint Basil, Fr. Vasile Mureșan, diocesan inspector and priest of the Cathedral, and all the faithful at the beginning of the year.

title: The Joyful Feast of the Nativity of the Lord in Westland, Michigan
intro:
“Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy which will be to all people. For there is born to you this day a Savior, who is Christ the Lord” (Luke 2, 10-11).

This is the great and joyful news that the angel of the Lord announced to the shepherds around Bethlehem at the Nativity of the Son of God as a human Child, of the Holy Spirit and of the Ever-Virgin Mary (Matthew 1, 18; Luke 1, 35): “For there is born to you this day a Savior, who is Christ the Lord” (Luke 2, 10-11), He who is a permanent today, who by divine providence has gladdened every generation for more than two thousand years at the Feast of the Nativity of the Child Jesus. This joy at the birth of a Savior, who is the Messiah, Christ the Lord, the One promised by God, brings not only the greatest joy but also the gift of spiritual rebirth through the faith of all of us, to the glory of God and the salvation of our souls.

Thus the gifts brought by the Magi to the Child Jesus, “gold, frankincense, and myrrh” (Matthew 2, 11), as to a King and God, help us understand where the presents come from that we give one another at the great feast of the Nativity of the Lord (Christmas), continuing the tradition of the Magi. And the greatest Gift, incomparably great, that God has given to mankind and to all generations out of His great love for the salvation of the world (John 3, 16) is His own Son, Jesus Christ, while the gift that the good God asks of man is his soul, through the Sacrament of Holy Baptism, so as to give him new birth of water and the Holy Spirit for the Kingdom of God (John 3, 5), and also through the Sacrament of Repentance in adulthood, after he has fallen into faults and sins, as the Lord says: “Repent, and believe in the gospel” (Mark 1, 15). All of this in fulfillment of the will of God.

By providence, and through the love and faith of the faithful for the Feast of the Nativity of the Lord, we too, the priest and faithful of “Saint Simeon” Romanian Orthodox Church in Westland, Michigan, gathered at the stable of Bethlehem of our time, which is the Church, beginning on the Eve of the Feast of the Nativity of the Child Jesus, on the day of the Nativity, on the second day for the Synaxis of the Mother of God, and on the third day for the feast of Saint Stephen the Archdeacon.

According to tradition, on the day of the Feast of the Nativity of the Child Jesus (Christmas), Santa Claus came with gifts for the children. Then, after the Divine Liturgy, the carol concert and Santa Claus’s visit to the children, the community stayed and rejoiced together in the Nativity of the Lord at the traditional Christmas meal with traditional dishes.

And so we thank our Savior Jesus Christ, who was born for us and for all, for this great joy this year of 2022 as well, at the Feast of His Nativity, and we wish everyone Many and Blessed Years in 2023 from Christ the Savior, for the wishes are in our power, but their fulfillment lies in the power and mercy of the good God.

Many and Blessed Years,

Fr. Aurel Sas

title: Christmas Celebration at “Saint Gregory the Theologian” Parish, Easley, SC
intro:
It is said of Christmas that it is nostalgia for the past, joy for the present and hope for the future. And since children are the extension of their parents, our Orthodox Church stays alive as long as we parents invest in our little ones of today, the Orthodox offshoots of tomorrow.

Together with the grown-ups, the little ones were present at the Divine Liturgy of the Nativity of the Lord. The children were very surprised, curious and happy when our parish priest, Fr. David Hudson, brought into his short catechesis for them real objects such as gold, myrrh and frankincense. The children could see, smell and touch these objects. The teaching method chosen with great care by our priest suited the children’s stage of psychological development and contributed greatly to their understanding of the biblical moment: “And when they had come into the house, they saw the young Child with Mary His mother, and fell down and worshiped Him. And when they had opened their treasures, they presented gifts to Him: gold, frankincense, and myrrh” (Matthew 2, 11).

The adults present at the Divine Liturgy understood that the authenticity of the precious gifts is supported on the one hand by oral tradition and on the other by history. But what undeniably confirms the authenticity of the precious gifts is their ineffable fragrance and their healing and wonderworking grace.

Since the tradition of caroling is handed down from generation to generation, this year too, after the Divine Liturgy, the children prepared a short artistic program of carols and poems for those present, all prepared under the careful and meticulous coordination of the parish teachers. The clear, gentle voices of the children recited in the sweet ancestral language the incomparable poems of Mihai Eminescu, Elena Farago and Traian Dorz, woven harmoniously together with traditional Christmas carols. The children offered the carols and verses from the heart while the angels smiled to hear them.

The feast of the Nativity of the Lord ended with a festive meal at which everyone enjoyed the fine dishes in very pleasant company. As they left for their homes, all the brothers and sisters in Christ were radiant with joy, for undoubtedly, as every year, Christmas waves its magic wand over the whole world and everything becomes gentler and more beautiful.

 

Reported by

Mihaela Livingston

title: Eminescu Honored in New York
intro:
As part of the series of events dedicated to honoring Romanian Culture Day and Mihai Eminescu, organized by the Academy of Romanian Scientists, American Branch, the UZPR Cultural Department, the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas and the Romanian Institute of Orthodox Theology and Spirituality in New York, the 30th edition of the “Mihai Eminescu” International Symposium took place on Saturday, January 14, in Astoria, New York, with the theme: Romanian Education and Culture Today. Assessment and Directions.

At the invitation of the organizer of this event, Fr. Prof. Dr. Theodor Damian, parish priest of “Holy Apostles Peter and Paul” Church, those who took part from Romania, directly on the Zoom platform, were Prof. Dr. Adrian Badea, president of the Academy of Romanian Scientists, academician Theodor Codreanu, university professors Nicolae Georgescu and Anca Sârghie, cultural journalist Marian Nencescu, and university professors  Doina Banciu, Ecaterina Andronescu, Vasile Sârbu, Ivan Cizmaru  and Sorin Ivan of the AOSR,  and from New York, ICR director Dorian Branea, university professor Valentina Ciaprazi of LaGuardia College, N.Y.,  and others. The Symposium was moderated by Prof. Nicole Smith, and technical assistance was provided by Andrei and Claudia Damian and Sorin Lazăr. Representatives of the local press were also present: reporter Cristi Boghian of  RomanianTv, New York, and photojournalist Alex Marmara of the magazine Lumină Lină/Gracious Light.

At the opening, following the academic protocol established by tradition by Fr. Prof. Theodor Damian, the guests and the audience sang the hymn Când a fost să moară Ștefan, in memory of the victory of Stephen the Great at the battle of Vaslui - Podul Înalt on January 10, 1475, the most brilliant Romanian victory against the Ottoman armies led by Suleiman Pasha, then the hymn Gaudeamus Igitur, and lyric artist  Lia Lungu performed live the song Rugăciune, on verses by Mihai Eminescu.

Addresses were given by Prof. Dr. Adrian Badea, president of the AOSR, and (read by Fr. Theodor Damian) His Eminence Dr. Nicolae Condrea, Romanian Orthodox Archbishop of the United States and Metropolitan of the Americas, headquartered in Chicago, both paying tribute to the personality of Mihai Eminescu, “a gift given by God to the Romanian people,” as His Eminence Metropolitan Dr. Nicolae Condrea emphasized in his Word of Blessing.

Then came the papers themselves, presented by:  Acad. Theodor Codreanu - Eminescu’s Philosophy and Its Implications for His Vision of the School, Prof. Dr. Nicolae Georgescu - Eminescology, an Interdisciplinary Science, Prof. Dr. Anca Sârghie - The “Real” School  as an Institution of Identity in the Vision of Mihai Eminescu the Journalist, Dr. Marian Nencescu - Eminescian Topicalities: The School, between Education and Culture, Fr. Prof. Dr. Theodor Damian - The Present-Day Relevance of Eminescu’s Vision of Education, and Prof. Valentina Ciaprazi - The Critique of Snobbish Imitation in the Poem “Ai noștri tineri” by Mihai Eminescu. Finally, literary critic Alex Ștefănescu   gave a pertinent and acid commentary on the poem Doina by Mihai Eminescu, in his opinion “a subversive reading” even today, as long as we do not grasp the real dimension of the drama of the Romanian nation, felt acutely by Eminescu and perpetuated to our own day.

At the close of the event, Lia Lungu performed the poem Revedere, on verses by Mihai Eminescu.

Comprehensive, original and suited to the theme, the papers presented at the Symposium highlighted either less known aspects of the biography of the National Poet, which deserve to be made public, if only to correct some “legends” that persist in our official criticism, or interpretations of Eminescu’s theses on the state and condition of Romanian education, and indirectly of the spiritual condition of the nation, a century ago and always. The idea was emphasized that, without being a pedagogue in the modern sense of the term, Mihai Eminescu also had a vast pedagogical culture, formed in his student years and consolidated in his brief experience as a teacher and, in administration, as a school reviewer/ inspector, all this knowledge and information being  developed  in his journalism, begun in Iași and continued for 6 years in Bucharest at the newspaper Timpul. Echoes of his pedagogical experience also show through in his literary work, in his poetry as well as in his fantastic novellas. In this context, the initiative of Fr. Prof. Theodor Damian to focus this year, within the “Mihai Eminescu” International Symposium, on aspects that also concern the Romanian school of today is not only welcome but also awaited, as a source of viable solutions, by many intellectuals concerned about the future of Romanian education.

 

Marian NENCESCU

title: Symposium on the Union of the Romanian Principalities, New York – 30th Edition
intro:
Every year for the last 30 years, the month of January has brought the Romanians of New York the joy of two important celebrations with a deep and welcome national character: the “Eminescu” Symposium in the middle of the month and then, a week later, the Symposium dedicated to the Union of the Romanian Principalities.

This year as well, after the academic event dedicated to the national poet Mihai Eminescu, attended by distinguished Eminescu scholars from Romania and from New York, the 30th academic Symposium dedicated to the Union of the Romanian Principalities took place on Sunday, January 22, 2023, at “Holy Apostles Peter and Paul” Church in that city, under the aegis of the Academy of Romanian Scientists, New York Branch, the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, the Union of Professional Journalists of Romania and the Romanian Institute of Orthodox Theology and Spirituality, New York, the de facto organizer of the event.

In the church’s social hall, Fr. Prof. Dr. Theodor Damian opened the gathering by briefly explaining the significance of the Union in the past and today, especially in a context in which love for one’s people and country, for one’s homeland, is very often regarded as a wrongdoing, the notion of nationalism being denied its positive, and in fact fundamental, connotation and given only a negative one, which always makes the subject appear delicate, if not risky.

The hymns “Când a fost să moară Ştefan”, “Basarabie frumoasă” and “Deşteaptă-te Române” were then sung, after which Prof. Nicole Smith, the moderator of the Symposium, introduced the speakers and the topics of their presentations in turn, as follows:

Fr. Prof. Dr. Theodor Damian, writer, President of the American Branch of the Academy of Romanian Scientists and of the Romanian Institute of Orthodox Theology and Spirituality, New York, Archimandrite Neofit Scriban on the Union and Non-Union of the Romanian Principalities; Prof. Dr. Doru Tsaganea, Professor of Mathematics at Metropolitan College of New York, The Union of the Romanian Principalities in the Context of the New Socio-Political Ideas Generated by the Revolutions of 1848; Prof. Valentina Ciaprazi, writer, Professor of French Language and Literature, LaGuardia College,  New York, If the Union Were to Happen under Today’s Conditions, Would It Still Be Achieved?; Cezar Ungureanu, graduate of the “Marist” Program, student at the School of Law, City University of New York, The Politics of the Romanian Question.

The beloved Bessarabian actress Maria Grecu then recited poems by Grigore Vieru and Dumitru Matcovschi, which the audience rewarded with warm applause.

Then everyone present joined in the moving Hora Unirii, group photos were taken and the conversations continued during the meal generously offered by the ladies of the Church committee.

Fr. Prof. Theodor Damian received much appreciation for organizing in New York such events, meant to keep Romanians’ awareness of their national belonging alive, so that they may rejoice in it, celebrate it and continue to grow in it.

Gh. Brehuescu

title: New Decisions of the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church
intro:
February 10, 2023

New Decisions of the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church

 

On Thursday, February 9, 2023, the working session of the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church was held in the “Teoctist Patriarhul” Aula Magna of the Patriarchal Palace, chaired by His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel.

The Holy Synod, by secret ballot, elected the Very Reverend Archimandrite Gherontie Ciupe as Auxiliary Bishop of the Diocese of Deva and Hunedoara. The new Auxiliary Bishop will bear the title His Grace Gherontie Hunedoreanul. His consecration as bishop will take place in Deva on Sunday, February 19, 2023.

At the same session, the following decisions were also made:

  1. Declaring 2024 in the Romanian Patriarchate the Homage Year of the Pastoral Care of the Sick and the Commemorative Year of All the Holy Unmercenary Healers;
  2. Approving the program of the International Meeting of Orthodox Youth (ITO – 2023), an event that will take place in Timișoara from August 31 to September 3, 2023;
  3. Approving the text of the Akathist to Saint Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia (December 2) and its inclusion in the liturgical books of the Romanian Orthodox Church;
  4. Approving the text of the Service of Saints Barsanuphius and John of Gaza (February 6) and its inclusion in the liturgical books of the Romanian Orthodox Church;
  5. Approving the recognition of the autocephaly granted to the Church in the Republic of North Macedonia under the name “Archdiocese of Ohrid and North Macedonia, with its see in Skopje”, by the Patriarchate of Serbia through the synodal Tomos issued on June 5, 2022. Its Primate will be commemorated with the title “His Beatitude Stefan, Archbishop of Ohrid, Skopje and North Macedonia”;
  6. Approving the organization throughout the Romanian Patriarchate of a collection for the victims of the recent earthquake in Turkey and Syria.

Regarding the situation of the Romanian Orthodox parishes in Northern Bukovina, which are under the jurisdiction of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church, the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church firmly maintains its position in favor of respecting the rights and freedoms of the Romanian communities throughout Ukraine, just as Ukrainians are respected throughout Romania.

The Holy Synod took note of the results of the social-philanthropic work of the Romanian Orthodox Church in 2022, amounting to 339,925,775 lei (approximately 69,000,000 euros), including 42,904,050 lei given to support refugees from Ukraine.

 

Press Office of the Romanian Patriarchate

title: Pastoral Letter of the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church for the Sunday of Orthodoxy in the Year of Our Lord 2023
intro:
Pastoral Letter of the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church on

the Sunday of Orthodoxy in the Year of Our Lord 2023

To the most venerable monastics, the most reverend clergy and the most beloved faithful throughout the Romanian Patriarchate,

Grace, joy and peace from God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and from us fatherly blessings!

Most Venerable and Most Reverend Fathers,
Beloved faithful,

After the first week of the Fast, in which we took part in the service of the Canon of Repentance of Saint Andrew of Crete, we experience on this Sunday, the Sunday of Orthodoxy, moments of spiritual joy, since at the Divine Liturgy we partake of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Ever since the apostolic period, the Church has had to face, for centuries on end, heresies and schisms, that is, deviations from the truth of the faith. Heretics and all those who fell into various errors caused division among Christians, some out of ignorance and others for personal reasons.

To stop these errors, the Church organized local synods, and when the heresies were seen to spread widely, the Ecumenical Councils were convened, attended by hierarchs from the whole Church.

Thus, from the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea in 325 to the Sixth Ecumenical Council of Constantinople in 680-681, the Church formulated and established essential truths of the teaching of the faith, such as: the divinity of the Son of God and of the Holy Spirit, the union of the divine nature and the human nature through the Incarnation of the Son of God, and the existence of two wills, corresponding to the two natures – human and divine – in the Person of the Savior Jesus Christ.

All these, however, were not mere theories or philosophical formulations. The Holy Fathers, inspired by God, understood that every teaching of the faith is directly connected with salvation, or the attaining of eternal life (cf. Matthew 5, 19). “If Christ is not God, He cannot deify me,” said Saint Athanasius the Great.

Right-believing Christians,

In the 8th century a new error appeared, according to which the veneration of icons and of holy relics was idolatry. In the face of it, eminent representatives of the Church showed that icons are not given the worship of adoration; rather, through their veneration, the holy persons painted and depicted on them are honored. It is not the material from which the icons are made that is venerated, but the saints whom the icons represent.

Emperors such as Leo III the Isaurian (717-741) and his son Constantine V Copronymus (741-775) waged a fierce struggle against icons. They ordered the removal of icons from the churches and from the homes of the faithful.

Works of great historical and artistic value were gathered and given over to the fire. During this period, many hierarchs, monks, priests and faithful who confessed the right veneration of the holy icons were mutilated, exiled and even killed.

Numerous monasteries were set on fire, demolished or turned into barracks. Paintings and mosaics were destroyed or covered with plaster. Under Leo IV the Khazar (775-780), many dignitaries who venerated icons were dismissed, mistreated, or sent to monasteries and forcibly tonsured monks. Empress Irene was also exiled because she venerated icons and sided with those who defended the veneration of icons.

In 780, after the death of Leo IV, Empress Irene became regent for her minor son, Constantine VI (780-797). Through her care, the Seventh Ecumenical Council was convened under the presidency of Patriarch Tarasios of Constantinople, in the Church of Hagia Sophia in Nicaea, in 787, and the veneration of icons was restored.

It was attended by 343 bishops, along with eminent representatives of the monks and of the parish clergy.

At this council the following teaching of the faith was formulated: “We keep unchanged all the ecclesiastical traditions, written or unwritten, entrusted to us, among which is also the iconic imprint through painting, which is in accord with the history of the Gospel proclamation, as an assurance that the becoming man of God the Word was real and not imaginary, and which brings us a similar benefit. […] This being so, proceeding on the royal path and following the God-inspired teaching of our Holy Fathers, as well as the Tradition of the Catholic Church, for we recognize that it is of the Holy Spirit who dwells in it, we decree with all exactitude and care that, like the figure of the precious and life-giving Cross, so too the venerable and holy icons, whether of colors or of mosaic or of any other suitable material, are to be set up in the holy churches of God, on the sacred vessels and vestments, on walls and on wood, in houses and by the roadsides; [namely] the icon of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ and of our Most Pure Lady, the Holy Theotokos, of the honorable angels and of all the saints and holy men. For the more frequently they are seen through iconic representation, the more those who behold them are lifted up to remember and to long for the prototypes, and to give them a kiss and reverent veneration. Not, however, true worship, which according to our faith belongs to the divine nature alone, but like that given to the figure of the precious and life-giving Cross, to the Holy Gospels and to the other sacred objects of worship; for their honor, incense will be offered and lights will be lit, according to the pious custom of the ancients. For the honor [given] to the icon passes to the prototype, and whoever venerates the icon venerates the hypostasis depicted in it”[1].

Shortly after this victory, the peace of the Church was disturbed again. Emperor Leo V the Armenian (813-820), although he had sworn an oath before the Patriarch that he would respect the decisions of the Seventh Ecumenical Council, proved to be an iconomach, that is, a new persecutor of icons. Icons and holy crosses were gathered and burned, and holy relics were destroyed.

Patriarch Nikephoros of Constantinople (806-815), author of two treatises against the iconoclasts, together with the bishops, abbots and monks who defended the icons, among them Saint Theodore the Studite, were removed, some of them being mistreated and killed.

Saint Theodore the Studite, abbot of the Stoudios Monastery, states very clearly that the veneration of the icon of Christ is directed toward the Person of Christ: “The icon of Christ is nothing other than Christ, obviously apart from the difference of essence, as has already been shown several times. That is why its veneration is also a veneration of Christ, since nothing of the material of the icon is venerated, but only Christ, who is portrayed in it. And things that have one likeness also have one veneration”[2].

Beloved spiritual sons and daughters,

In 843, when Empress Theodora convened a synod in Constantinople, the decisions of the seven Ecumenical Councils and the veneration of icons were confirmed, and Patriarch Methodios of Constantinople (843-847) proclaimed the victory of the Church over all the heresies of the first eight centuries.

He composed a Synodikon, in which he set out the Orthodox teaching, condemning all heresies, and ordered the restoration of the veneration of icons in the holy churches. On March 11, 843, at the hierarchical Divine Liturgy celebrated in the Hagia Sophia Cathedral in Constantinople, Patriarch Methodios made it publicly known that the first Sunday of Great Lent would be called the Sunday of Orthodoxy, that is, of the right faith.

On the Sunday of Orthodoxy, the victory of the Church over all heresies is celebrated year after year, and those who remained faithful to the Church in times of great trial are commemorated.

In Holy Scripture there are numerous proofs that highlight the duty of each of us to venerate the holy icons. Already in the first chapter of the Book of Genesis it is said that God created man in His image and likeness (cf. Genesis 1, 26-27). Therefore, man was created according to the image (icon) of God.

God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that the world might have life, and have it more abundantly (cf. John 3, 16; 10, 10). Therefore, the Son of God became incarnate and became Man, for He is the icon of the Father (cf. Hebrews 1, 2-3).

That is why Jesus Christ Himself said: “He who has seen Me has seen the Father” (John 12, 45; 14, 9). Saint John of Damascus refers to the depiction of God in an icon, saying: “I depict the invisible God, not as invisible, but as One who became visible for us by partaking of flesh and blood. I do not depict the invisible divinity, but I depict the visible Body of God”[3].

The holy icons painted in our churches have been the bible of the unlettered, for they have an important role in increasing Christian piety.

The icon is a means of better understanding the work of salvation brought by the Savior Jesus Christ. “We do not err when we make the icon of God who became incarnate, who appeared on earth in the flesh and dwelt among men, who, out of His ineffable goodness, took on the nature, materiality, form and color of the body”[4].

Pious Christians have venerated the icons representing the Great Feasts, the Mother of God, and the icons depicting the faces of the saints. Present at the Divine Liturgies, the services and the rites celebrated in our churches, the faithful grow in piety thanks to the spiritual presence of the saints painted in the icons.

The iconostasis, as a support for special icons symbolizing the Kingdom of Heaven, helps the believer enter into communion with God and with His saints. Each person’s mind is illumined by seeing the light of Christ’s presence, and the heart rejoices. The joy of the Orthodox believer continues at home, where, before the icons on the eastern wall, he says his private prayers.

Beloved brothers and sisters in the Lord,

An icon can be a beautiful and choice gift for those close to us: relatives, friends, colleagues or acquaintances, on the occasion of various moments in their lives, such as birthdays or name days. By giving Holy Icons, Bibles, Psalters or Prayer Books, we perform deeds well-pleasing to God.

Likewise, a good deed of great worth is almsgiving to those in need, the suffering or the sick who have no one left. By supporting parish churches or monasteries, like the founders, the faithful princes or boyars of the past of our ancestral Church, we perform deeds that are written in the Book of Life. These good deeds are the spiritual dowry, or the light of our soul in eternal life.

In this sense, the Savior Jesus Christ commanded: “Be merciful, just as your Father also is merciful!” (Luke 6, 36). In the Book of the Acts of the Apostles we read that “Cornelius’ prayers and alms have come up for a memorial before God” (Acts of the Apostles 10, 4).

Saint Basil the Great, referring to acts of almsgiving, states that they remain accounted before the Throne of the Most Holy Trinity. Whoever gives of his little to the poor becomes spiritually rich: “You gave to the hungry; but what you gave remains yours and returns to you with increase”[5].

That is why, seven decades ago, the Romanian Orthodox Church established that on the Sunday of Orthodoxy a collection called the Central Missionary Fund be taken in all the churches of the Romanian Patriarchate. The sums collected have been and are used to carry out social assistance and philanthropic projects and programs.

There is still a need to support the places of worship and the social institutions belonging to the Church. Through this fund, some Romanian communities outside the country’s borders will also be supported, especially those that do not have a place of worship.

Let each of us strive to contribute to this collection according to our means, bearing in mind the words of Saint John Chrysostom: “Whatever those who give alms ask of God, they immediately receive the gift of their request. Such honor and boldness before God does almsgiving have, that it not only washes away the sins of the merciful, but even drives away death, and it is proven that almsgiving rules over all things and conquers death”[6].

Let us use the time of the Fast of Holy Pascha to grow in prayer and good deeds, hoping that we will rejoice spiritually in the Great Feast of the Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ.

We embrace you with fatherly love and pray that “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God the Father, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all!” (2 Corinthians 13, 13).

President of the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church

title: The Sunday of Orthodoxy at Annunciation Church in Olmsted Township, Ohio
intro:
The First Sunday of Great Lent, the Sunday of Orthodoxy, at Annunciation Church in Olmsted Township, Ohio, reminds us every year of God’s victory over the false models of this world, ever since the 9th century. We have this Sunday as an undying example across the ages that the Holy Icons and the Grace that flows from them prove the reality of the presence in the flesh of the Son of God in the world, born of the Virgin Mary. It also reminds us of the honor enjoyed by the friends of God, who through union with Him overcame the world and its idols, themselves becoming living icons of the Living God. And further, it reminds us of the call made to all of us to become living icons ourselves, apostles, models, the light of the world that lives in the darkness of the false models of this world, which seems ruled more and more by the hater of icons. May the good God help us all fulfill this calling!

Glory to God for all things!

Fr. Petru Neaga

title: Children’s Liturgy at the Parish of Saint John Cassian and Saint Andrei Șaguna, Metropolitan of Transylvania
intro:
For the sixth year in a row, the Divine Liturgy was celebrated with the young people and children of Saint John Cassian Parish. This is a special Liturgy, served twice a year, during Great Lent and during the Nativity Fast, only with and for the children. The ladies of the parish school were there alongside the children.

The children, young and old, took an active part in the Liturgy. Fr. Valentin performed the Proskomedia in the middle of the church, surrounded by the children. They had the opportunity to observe in detail how the Proskomedia is carried out, and they were the ones who commemorated the living and the departed of their families. It is an opportunity for the young people and children to unite in one voice and one soul at this holy and moving moment. The Liturgy continued with the young people and children singing and actively taking part in the Divine Liturgy.

After the Divine Liturgy, the participants had lunch together with Father and the ladies of the parish school. The day continued with crafts such as making cards, beaded eggs, painting on wood and a special project created by each child. On a large sheet, each child drew a cross divided into 40 squares, each representing a day of Great Lent. Each Sunday is identified and marked with a drawing and a text. For example, the Sunday of Orthodoxy has an icon next to it, the Sunday of the Holy Cross has a cross next to it, and so on. This project will continue every Sunday of Lent until it is fully completed, on the first Sunday of Pascha. Fr. Valentin also dedicates this day to the confession of the children and young people.

Another activity that has already become a tradition is the chess competition. This year, the young people first had the chance to teach the little ones chess. After that, the chess competition among the parish youth took place.

The Children’s Liturgy is an opportunity for the little ones, and also for the teenagers of the parish, to take an active part in the Liturgy, to spend time together and to practice virtues such as faith, kindness and patience, as well as compassion, love of neighbor and understanding.

Glory to God for all things!

Adina Pasnicu

title: The First Orthodox Baptism in Cancun
intro:
A pastoral emergency provided the occasion for an extremely important meeting for the future of the Romanian community in Cancun, Mexico. From May 10 to 13, 2023, Fr. Daniel Ene, Eparchial Secretary and Dean of New York, New England and the Eastern USA, was in Mexico with the blessing of His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae, at the invitation of the Romanian community of the state of Quintana Roo.

On Wednesday, May 10, Fr. Daniel took part in the meeting of the Romanian community of Cancun with His Excellency Mr. Marius Gabriel Lazurcă, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Romania to Mexico, on the occasion of the visit of a delegation from Romania to the Mexican Federation, a delegation headed by Mr. Valentin Muntean, Director General of the Consular Department of the Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Mr. Claudiu Băjenaru, Deputy Director General in the Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs, also attended the meeting.

Only two days later, on Friday, May 12, Fr. Daniel performed the first baptism in the midst of the Romanian community of Cancun. The young Mateo Degeratu De La Rosa received the Sacrament of Holy Baptism and the Sacrament of Chrismation, the first Orthodox baptism performed in Cancun. On the evening of the same day, Fr. Daniel met with the Roman Catholic Bishop of Cancun and Chetumal, Msgr. Pedro Pablo Elizondo Cárdenas, with whom he again discussed the possibility of obtaining a space on loan for use at the Sanctuary of Saint Mary in Cancun, in order to build the first Orthodox church in this area.

Saturday morning was the time for the Divine Liturgy in Romanian IN CANCUN (PLAYA DEL CARMEN). The Divine Liturgy was celebrated by Fr. Daniel Ene and Fr. Iulian Aniței (Houston TX). The service took place at the Catholic church of Saint Mary in Cancun (Santuario Maria Desatadora de Nudos - Av 145 SM320 Polígono Sur Jardines del Sur, 77536 Cancún, Q.R., Mexico). Through the kindness of Fr. Luis and with the permission of the Catholic Diocese of Cancun, the Holy Service was celebrated in one of the chapels of this beautiful property.  https://www.facebook.com/Santuario-Maria-Desatadora-de-Nudos-1924907117733597/

A large number of faithful took part in the Divine Liturgy, rejoicing in the presence of the priests and in the opportunity of opening the first Romanian parish in Mexico and the first Orthodox church in Quintana Roo (Cancun, Playa del Carmen, Tulum, Riviera Maya). A family from the community, present at this Divine Liturgy, offered to donate the entire construction of a wooden church in the event of an agreement on the land between the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas and the Catholic Diocese of Cancun. At Fr. Daniel’s proposal, the wish of all those present was that the church be dedicated to Saint Joseph the Confessor, Bishop of Maramureș (April 24).

Reported by

Fr. Daniel Ene
