title: The Feast of the Annunciation in Seattle, Washington
intro:
A day of joy in prayer and national feeling for the Romanians of Saints Joachim and Anna Parish in Seattle on the feast of the Annunciation. Good tidings and a joyful reunion for a community of faithful made up of brothers and sisters from both sides of the Prut, separated for a time by a border but united forever in faith, in language and in bright hopes.

We Orthodox Romanians gathered together in the Divine Liturgy under the care of our chief shepherd, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, who came to visit his rational flock, to pray with us, to listen to us and to guide us. Dressed in traditional costume, with Greater Romania in our hearts, we found peace and felt at home, knowing that no water separates us from our people, neither the Atlantic Ocean nor the Prut. Here, far from Romanian lands, we live with longing for our people and our ancestral land, and we take comfort in fragments of Romania carried in traditional dress, in the doina, in dance, in lament and in the hope of returning home to our own. That is precisely why the Church remains a spiritual haven for each of us, a mystical place where we sit at table with God, where we weep and smile, where we calm souls wearied by longing and trials, renew our minds in confession and receive renewed hope. Here we are all at home, in the house of the Lord.

In his homily, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae spoke to us about the feast of the Annunciation, about the commemoration of Saint Mary of Egypt, and about the living Church, which lives by partaking of the source of Life, Christ, through participation and presence at the Liturgy, through Orthodox apostolate, and through an authentic and exemplary life. He then spoke about the canonization of Saint Joseph the Merciful and Saint George the Pilgrim at the blessed moment of the celebration of 100 years since the Union of Bessarabia with Romania.

Each of us can be or become an apostle, a missionary, a sower of joy and of healing faith in a world drifting ever further from God. The Liturgy of the Church then continues in the efforts of each of us, in the witness of our lives, in our dedication and our sacrifice. There are still many brothers and sisters who have not found the way to the Church, perhaps out of weariness, too much concern with the things of this world, forgetfulness or ignorance. Our example, our love and our refusal to judge can bring them together with Christ.

After the Divine Liturgy we all gathered, Romanians from this side and the other side of the Prut, remembering and reliving the Great Union accomplished in 1918. We sang the national anthem and recalled several important moments in the turbulent history of Greater Romania.

The “Datina” folk ensemble delighted us with beautiful ancestral customs, songs and brotherly hora dances, a comfort to souls far from home. This ensemble strives to preserve ancestral customs, Romanian traditions and the faith of our forefathers, here, far from home, but with longing and love for Romania.

Humble thanks to God for the grace and blessing of our joy! A warm bow to His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, who carries with us the longing for home and the longing for salvation!

Fr. Ionuț Silvestru Țurcă

title: Anniversary of the Union of Bessarabia with Romania at Saint Simeon Romanian Orthodox Church in Westland, Michigan
intro:
After the Divine Liturgy on Sunday, March 25, 2018, we celebrated 100 years since the historic Union of Bessarabia with Romania on March 27, 1918, after the First World War.

On this blessed occasion, a Parastas was held for the heroes and makers of the Great Union of Bessarabia with the Motherland, as well as a Te Deum service of thanksgiving to the Good God for the anniversary, followed at the end by the “Many Years” wishes, according to the rubrics.

Fr. Aurel Sas delivered a homily on this great event, showing how after 106 years Bessarabia returned to union with Romania on March 27, 1918, thus fulfilling the joy revealed by the Scriptures: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” (Psalm 132, 1). “…for there the Lord commanded the blessing, life forevermore” (Psalm 132, 3).

After the homily, all the faithful present, in good number, gathered at the festive meal specially prepared for the great celebration, in honor of this great anniversary. The centennial celebration ended with a look ahead to the celebration on December 1, 2018, of the Union of the other provinces of the country with the Motherland.

Many years, Romania!

Fr. Aurel Sas

title: The Feast of the Lord’s Resurrection in New York
intro:
The Resurrection of the Lord is the greatest and oldest feast of Christendom, the day of our joy and of our hope in eternity. The Resurrection of the Lord is God’s gift to us, a holy joy we feel deep in our hearts and confess by saying “Christ is risen!”, to which we answer: “Truly He is risen!”

With this thought in mind, the Romanians of the Saint Nicholas and Saint George Parish in New York welcomed the feast of the Lord’s Resurrection this year as well. As always, hundreds of Romanian faithful, joined by small groups of Greeks and Russians, came at midnight to receive the Holy Light. Faith in the Lord’s Resurrection united all those present in one mind and one voice.

Shortly before midnight, the candles in the hands of the faithful were lit from the Holy Light offered by the parish priest. On a stage set up in front of the church, the Resurrection service began with the reading of the Holy Gospel, followed by the reading of the message of our Archpastor, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae. At the end, Fr. Marius Dumitrescu urged the faithful to be good and true confessors of Orthodoxy and thanked everyone present.

The liturgical program then continued in the church with Matins and the Divine Liturgy, attended by many of those who had come before midnight. To the glory of God and to our joy, a large number of faithful received Holy Communion at the Divine Liturgy. The service was also attended by the Deputy Prime Minister of Romania, Mrs. Ana Birchall, and the Consul General of Romania in New York, Mr. Cătălin Radu Dancu.  The service concluded with the traditional Paschal agape meal.

Fr. Marius Dumitrescu

title: Holy Pascha at Saint Simeon Romanian Orthodox Church in Westland, MI
intro:
Christ is risen! Truly He is risen!
Come, receive the Light!

With this call, addressed by the priest from the doors of the Holy Altar to all the faithful in the church to come and receive the light, according to the holy tradition of the Orthodox Church, the Resurrection service also began at Saint Simeon Romanian Orthodox Church in Westland, Michigan, at 12:00 am (midnight) on April 8, in the year of our Lord 2018.

After this call, made three times, for all those inside and outside the church to come and receive the light, Fr. Aurel Sas began the hymn “Thy Resurrection, O Christ our Savior…” together with the church choir, and they went out among the faithful with the Holy Cross, the Holy Gospel and the Icon of the Resurrection in procession around the church. After the procession, Fr. Aurel began the Resurrection service with the reading of the Holy Gospel, followed by the rest of the service, everything culminating in the hymn Christ is risen!

Then, following the tradition of the priest’s call before the doors of the church, “Lift up your gates, O you princes, and the King of glory shall come in…”, everyone entered the church to continue the service with readings from the Canon of the Resurrection and the celebration of the Divine Liturgy, to the glory of God and the salvation of the people. Before Holy Communion, Fr. Aurel Sas read to the faithful the Paschal Pastoral Letter of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae.

At the end of the Divine Liturgy, Father presented several of the Lord’s appearances after His Resurrection from the dead, which confirm the event of Christ’s Resurrection as a unique fact in human history, and explained briefly that the Resurrection of Christ is the guarantee that all generations will rise to new life from the spiritual death of sin through faith in Christ’s Resurrection from the dead.

The truth of the Resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead is an undeniable truth, because it is confirmed by His appearances after the Resurrection, which culminated in His appearance to over five hundred people at once in Jerusalem, who saw Him and recognized Him (1 Cor. 15, 6). Just as no historical fact seen by more than 500 people is disputed in history, all the more can the fact and truth of Christ’s Resurrection not be disputed, especially since the faith of generations in the truth of Christ’s Resurrection changes and renews their lives.

Fr. Aurel then thanked the families who donated the Holy Pascha, the Resurrection candle for the service and all the traditional Easter foods. Fr. Aurel Sas especially thanked all the faithful for their donations toward the building of the church’s iconostasis, of which two sections could already be seen: the one with the Icon of the Savior and the one with the Icon of the Mother of God with the Child Jesus.

After all the thanks and announcements, Fr. Aurel invited all the faithful to receive the Holy Pascha and to share the traditional Easter meal of lamb, red eggs, Romanian cozonac and other delicacies of Romanian cuisine. He also invited the faithful to the Vespers of the Resurrection at 11:00 am on Easter Day.

One thing that could be seen with great joy at the Paschal Resurrection service was that all the faithful (more than 120) stayed until the end of the service, after 2:00 am. Many also attended the Vespers of the Resurrection, even though this had not been a tradition in the parish.

This is how Holy Pascha was celebrated at Saint Simeon Church in Westland, MI, on this day “…which the Lord has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it” (Psalm 117, 24). We give thanks to the good God and to our Metropolitan, His Eminence Nicolae, for his blessing and care, and to the members of the Parish Council who helped organize everything for Holy Pascha.

Let us give our life a chance through faith in the Resurrection of Christ the Lord, the guarantee of our resurrection, to the glory of God and for salvation in Christ, Who rose from the dead on the third day according to the Scriptures (1 Cor. 15, 4) and Who assured us that He will be with us always (Matthew 28, 20). In this way we will be able to kindle the spiritual light of our souls from the divine and uncreated Light of Christ’s Resurrection, through faith in the truth of His Resurrection, and we will be able to have the Lord with us all the days of our life, unto salvation.

Christ is risen!

Fr. Aurel Sas

title: The Resurrection of the Lord in the Atlanta Area
intro:
The Romanian Orthodox community of St. Mary’s Church, whose patronal feast is the Protection of the Mother of God, in the Atlanta area celebrated the Resurrection of the Lord together with the entire Orthodox world. Throughout Holy Week, the holy church was adorned with black vestments. The Bridegroom Matins services, the Lamentations of the Lord and all the services of the Passion of the Savior prepared us spiritually, through repentance and forgiveness, for the bright feast of the Resurrection.

Although it rained early in the evening, and after the rain came a cold spell unusual for the Atlanta area, the church filled with faithful starting at 11:30 PM. As midnight approached, for a brief moment, darkness enveloped the entire church. Only the words of the Matins of Great and Holy Saturday echoed within the darkened walls of the church. At 12:00 midnight, Fr. Nicolae Clempuș brought us the light from the lampada on the Holy Altar. At the call of Christ, “Come, receive the light!” all the faithful partook of the light of the Holy Resurrection, and the church was illumined through them and their lit candles. After the procession around the church, the Holy Gospel of the Resurrection was read from a specially prepared place, after which the saving words “Christ is risen!” resounded. More than 400 faithful holding lit candles took part with deep emotion in receiving the Holy Light at midnight.

The service continued in the church with the Canon of the Resurrection and the Divine Liturgy, with the blessing of the “Pascha” bread and of the baskets of food brought by the faithful. Those who stayed until 3:30 AM cracked eggs and tasted the treats prepared for Pascha. We give glory to God for the blessings He has poured out upon us this year, 2018, as well.

Christ is risen! Truly He is risen!

Fr. Nicolae Clempuș

title: Pascha Night 2018, Holy Trinity Church, Rochester, NY
intro:
The church is adorned with flower arrangements in the windows, fragrant white lilies stand beneath every icon of the iconostasis, and baskets of traditional dishes rest on the table. People wait in whispers for the time to come. The pews slowly fill during the Canon. Then, as if at a signal, the lights go out and, in the stir of expectation, Fr. Daniel, holding a lit candle, calls us to receive the light. The light from the Holy Sepulchre, kept with love and care for a whole year on the Holy Table of the altar. As soon as we receive it, we pass it on, sharing it with our neighbors.

Outside the church the weather is freezing, colder than ever, it seems. But this does not keep us from awaiting the renewal of the good news: Christ is risen! Strong and joyful is our answer: Truly He is risen! And after the “leaders” opened the gates, we went back into the church. Those who could took part in the Divine Liturgy and received Holy Communion, then we went down to the social hall, where we shared the food we had brought and cracked eggs together.

Christ is risen!

Fr. Daniel Adrian Ene

title: Romania’s Centenary: Cornerstone Laid at Life-Giving Spring Church, Long Valley, New Jersey
intro:
On the Second Sunday after Pascha (of Saint Thomas the Apostle), His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas was in the midst of the faithful of Life-Giving Spring Parish in Long Valley, New Jersey, in the Deanery of New York, New England and the Eastern USA. The joy of His Eminence’s pastoral visit began on Saturday afternoon with a meeting with the members of the Parish Council and of the construction and marketing departments for the new wooden church. It continued in the evening with Great Vespers, served together with Dean Fr. Daniel Ene, Protosyngellos Vincențiu Temirov, Fr. Marius Lazăr, Fr. Mircea Airinei and the parish priest, Fr. Ionuț Voicu.

On Sunday morning, the clergy and a large number of faithful welcomed His Eminence Nicolae to the ringing of the bells and the singing of “Pre Stăpânul”. After the Divine Liturgy, in his homily to the faithful, His Eminence spoke about confessing faith in the Lord’s Resurrection, urging them to courage and joy, after the words of the Risen Christ to the myrrh-bearing women, in completing the building of the Maramureș-style wooden church. The parish priest thanked His Eminence Nicolae, the delegation of the Consulate of Romania in New York, Consul General Cătălin Dancu, who, though unable to attend, was actively involved in this project, the priests present, the parish members, and the donors and supporters of this project.

After the Divine Liturgy, the service of blessing the cornerstone was held for the Maramureș-style wooden church that will be built this year, to the glory of God and the joy of the Romanians in the state of New Jersey, USA, marking in this way as well the Centenary of Greater Romania.

A fellowship meal, prepared through the sacrifice and effort of our parish Ladies’ Committee in honor of all those who took part in this very important moment in the life of our community, concluded a day of great celebration. The visit of our Archpastor is always an occasion of joy. This time, as it coincided with His Eminence’s birthday, the faithful of the parish had the special joy of offering him their good wishes and singing “Many years!”. Before leaving, His Eminence Nicolae blessed the faithful, urging them to finish the work they have begun and to support and help with the building of the new holy place of worship.

Life-Giving Spring Parish was founded in July 2011 with the approval of the Eparchial Council of the Romanian Orthodox Archdiocese in the Americas. For a time, services were held at Saints Peter and Paul Orthodox Church in Rockaway, NJ (American Carpatho-Russian Orthodox Diocese). In May 2016, the papers were signed for the purchase of the parish’s own place of worship in Long Valley, NJ. Since then, the community has continued to grow and to fulfill ever more fittingly its mission to the Romanian Orthodox faithful in the state of New Jersey.

Fr. Ionuț Voicu

title: Triple Celebration in New York
intro:
For any Christian community, the patronal feast is a special day of celebration on which the patron saints of the church are honored. The Third Sunday after Pascha, of the Holy Myrrh-bearing Women, was a truly special one for the Romanian faithful of the parish of Saint Nicholas and Saint George in New York. They celebrated the second patron of the church, the Holy Great Martyr George.

The events dedicated to the patronal feast began on Saturday evening with the celebration of Vespers and continued the next day with Matins and the Sacrament of Holy Baptism joined with the Divine Liturgy, in which parish priest Fr. Marius Dumitrescu and Protosyngellos Vincențiu Temirov of Saint Demetrios the New Monastery in Middletown, NY took part. The baptism of the infant Thomas Justin Trepca was a reason for great joy for the family and also for our parish. At the end of the Divine Liturgy, a memorial service was held for the founders of the church.

After the service, all the faithful took part in the fellowship meal prepared by a group of families from our church. In this way, too, we were able to contribute to strengthening and perfecting the mystical bond created through prayer among those who strive to follow our Lord Jesus Christ.

During the fellowship meal, the first cultural event dedicated to the Centennial of the Great Union took place, symbolically titled “The Great Union of 1918 in the Consciousness of Romanians”. We note that this year, under the patronage of Saint Nicholas and Saint George Church, NY, a series of three cultural events will be held dedicated to the celebration of 100 years since the Great Union.

Prof. Dr. Nicholas Andronescu gave a lecture titled “The Union among Romanians”, and Eng. Cristian F. Pascu, president of the Dorul Christian Society, presented two topics: “A Romanian Hero: Samoilă Mârza – the Photographer of the Great Union” and “An Original and Unique Romanian Symbol in the USA: the Centennial Medal of the Dorul Romanian Christian Society”. The presentations were accompanied by photo and video projections.

The patronal feast celebration ended with a concert of patriotic folk songs performed by soloist Iuliana Roată. In closing, it only remains for us to extend our heartfelt thanks to those who took part and to all who prepared this feast of our church. May the Good God reward their love and sacrifice!

Fr. Marius Dumitrescu, Parish Priest

title: First Service in Romanian in Santiago de Chile, Blessing of the Romanian Embassy, Meeting with the Romanian Community
intro:
From February 26 to March 2, 2018, with the blessing of His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae, Fr. Daniel Ene, Eparchial Secretary and Dean of New York, New England and the Eastern United States, visited the Romanian community of Santiago de Chile and its surroundings at the invitation of the Embassy of Romania in the Republic of Chile.

Every stop in the world of Latin America is a unique experience, but Chile is a feast of experiences you will surely not see or live anywhere else on the globe. Stretched out along the coast of South America, Chile offers complex landscapes: from the drama of the Atacama Desert, coastal cities and green vineyards to the uniqueness of Patagonia and the Strait of Magellan.

The number of Romanian citizens settled in the Republic of Chile is approximately 2,000. Most of them live in Santiago de Chile and in Copiapo, a mining town where the number of Romanians is estimated at 500, and the rest in other cities such as Rancagua, Iquique, Valdivia, Valparaiso, Viña del Mar, Punta Arenas or Concepcion. It is a community made up mostly of professionals who came to Chile on work contracts or of family members of Chilean citizens. In recent years, a great many Romanians from Venezuela, frightened by the difficult and dangerous situation in the country where they lived,  have chosen Chile as their home because of the stability and prosperity of this country.

For all these Romanians and others as well, since there are also many descendants of Romanian citizens who came to Chile in the first decades of the last century or after the Second World War, most of whom were born in Chile and no longer hold Romanian citizenship, the Embassy of Romania in Santiago de Chile has been and remains a “little piece” of Romanian land that has eased their longing for home and for Romanian traditions.

Fr. Daniel Ene stepped into this authentically Romanian world and was welcomed with great love by Her Excellency Mrs. Monica Mihaela Știrbu, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Romania to the Republic of Chile, and by the embassy family. Love, patriotism, professionalism and determination are some of the qualities with which God has endowed the ambassador, qualities evident in all that she has managed to accomplish in a very short time. The Romanian embassy building, restored and returned to its former beauty, provided the occasion for its blessing in this year of the Centennial of Greater Romania.

And so, on Wednesday, February 28, in the afternoon, the festivities connected with the Centennial of Romania began. The service of blessing of the embassy building was followed by a Te Deum service and the blessing of the Romanian flag, attended by many Romanians. In his homily, the Dean conveyed the blessing of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae and urged the Romanians to keep their faith, language and Romanian tradition alive.

On the same occasion, a ceremony was held at the embassy for granting Romanian citizenship to a group of 6 Chileans, descendants of Romanian citizens who emigrated to Chile several decades ago. The national anthem and the oath they took gave the whole celebration a sense of meaning and fulfillment.

During the 5 days spent in Chile, Fr. Daniel Ene had frequent spiritual meetings, initiated by the Consul of Romania in Santiago de Chile, Mr. Florin Marian Palade, and by Mr. Andrei Știrbu.

On Tuesday, February 27, Fr. Daniel Ene also met with Fr. Ignatios Cavieres, Vicar of the Greek Orthodox Church in Santiago de Chile. The pastoral care of Romanians and the difficulties and particularities of Orthodoxy in Chile were among the topics discussed. At Fr. Daniel’s request, the Vicar committed to supporting the Romanian community pastorally and showed openness to a Romanian church presence in Santiago, being willing to allow a Romanian priest to celebrate the Divine Liturgy in Romanian in the Greek church of the Chilean capital.

Following this encouraging message, and the wish of all present that there should one day be a Romanian parish in Chile, Fr. Daniel Ene asked Mrs. Ioana Galea, a member of the community, to begin the steps toward founding a Romanian Orthodox Christian association as well as a Romanian school, assuring her of the full support of the Metropolia and of the Education Commission.

On Thursday, March 1, Fr. Daniel Ene also visited the contemporary art exhibition Anatomia Spiralei by Romanian artist Camil Mihăescu at the Baburizza Palace in Valparaiso, on the shore of the Pacific Ocean, an exhibition organized by the Embassy of Romania in Santiago de Chile in partnership with the City Hall of Valparaiso and in collaboration with the Valparaiso Museum of Fine Arts, the West University of Timișoara and the Association of Winegrowers of the Casablanca-Valparaiso Region.

The first visit of a representative of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas among the Romanian community of Chile was a fruitful occasion, thanks above all to the care and support of the ambassador and her collaborators, Consul Florin Palade, the Adriana and Virgil Macovei - Leurdean family, and the one whose humility and professionalism keep everything in perfect order, Andrei Știrbu.

It is hard to put one’s impression of Chile into a single sentence, but we can say that it is a civilized, modern country with professional people and clear rules… a TRUE PEARL at the end of the world.

Fr. Dean Daniel Ene

title: Religion Olympiad 2018
intro:
With the blessing of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas and of His Grace Bishop Ioan Casian, Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Canada,  on Sunday, April 29, 2018, the final stage of the eighth Religion Olympiad, 2018 edition, took place in six metropolitan centers in the USA and Canada and two special centers. The written parish round was taken by 151 children, and 77 contestants took part in the parishes that hosted the metropolitan-center round: 52 in the 8-12 age group and 25 young people in the 13-18 age group.

The tests were based on the new 2017-2018 curriculum of the parish schools. Thanks are due to the Education Committee of our Holy Metropolia, which organized and prepared the tests, especially Mr. Stelian Ghinea of Rochester NY and Mrs. Ileana Gavriș and Mrs. Veronica Ciocan of Edmonton AB, to the teachers in the two grading centers, and to all the teachers on the parish and metropolitan-center committees involved in this edition. A word of appreciation is also due to the eight parishes that joyfully hosted the eighth edition of the Religion Olympiad.

The prize winners will receive their diplomas from our hierarchs at the Congresses of the two dioceses, and the first-place winners in each category received a free voucher to attend the Metropolia’s summer camp in Allegan MI.

title: Events at Saints Peter and Paul Parish, New York
intro:
Throughout 2018, the year dedicated to the Centennial of Greater Romania, various events have taken place and will take place under the patronage of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Great Union.

To this end, at Saints Peter and Paul Parish, shepherded by Fr. Theodor Damian, and through the Romanian Institute of Orthodox Theology and Spirituality in New York, a special anniversary event dedicated to the Union of Bessarabia with Romania of March 27, 1918 was held on Sunday, March 25, 2018. The guest was Mr. Gabriel Gherasim of New York, who gave a lecture on the theme Romania between the Prut and the Dniester. His Excellency Cătălin Radu Dancu, Consul General of Romania in New York, was also invited to this festive occasion.

On Thursday, April 22, 2018, the same parish hosted a round table on the Treaty of Peace of Bucharest (April 24, 1919), marking 100 years since its partial signing. The guest of the event was Prof. Dr. Doru Tsaganea, and the moderator was Fr. Theodor Damian.

On Sunday, May 13, 2018, Saints Peter and Paul Parish in New York invites all who wish to take part in a program commemorating Romania’s State Independence Day, Monarchy Day and Mother’s Day according to the American tradition. Speakers at this event will be: Rev. Prof. Dr. Theodor Damian, Commentary on and presentation of the unionist letter of a priest from Banat, November 1918; His Excellency Cătălin Radu Dancu, Consul General of Romania in New York, Words of welcome on the great events celebrated; Prof. Dr. Doru Tsaganea, The significance of the two historical events, with emphasis on the role of King Ferdinand in the reunification of Romania; Dr. Napoleon Săvescu, The Union as reunification; and Prof. Mariana Terra, From Burebista to Ferdinand the Unifier. These addresses will be followed by a recital of music and poetry dedicated to mothers, and then by traditional Romanian and modern dances.

Fr. Prof. Theodor Damian

title: Celebration of the Centennial of Greater Romania, Victor, New York
intro:
All Saints Sunday, June 3, 2018, was an occasion of great celebration for the Romanian community of central and western New York State. His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was present among the faithful of Holy Trinity Parish in Rochester/Victor, NY.

His Eminence celebrated the Hierarchical Divine Liturgy together with Dean Fr. Daniel Ene, the parish priest of this church. At the end of the Divine Liturgy, a memorial service was held for the founders of the church, as well as for the makers of the Union of 1918 and all who labored for the unity of faith and nation of the Romanian people. In his homily, His Eminence spoke about the fact that today the Orthodox Church of Christ commemorates not one saint, not two, not ten, not a hundred, but all the saints. Then, by explaining the service of the Proskomedia, Metropolitan Nicolae spoke of the shared work of all the saints in the Church of Christ. The Holy Angels, the Martyrs, the Hierarchs, the Venerable Fathers and Mothers, together with the greatest intercessor of all, the Mother of God, protect us from all the hardships and trials that befall us. The faithful present at the holy services were able to venerate the holy relics kept in this church (the hand of Saint Empress Theodora of Byzantium, relics of Saint John Maximovitch, of the Holy Great Martyr Catherine, of the holy and righteous Anna, mother of the Virgin Mary, of the Holy Martyr Ephraim the New, as well as a vestment of Saint Philothea of Curtea de Argeș.

Immediately after the Divine Liturgy, in front of the wayside cross in the church garden, a Te Deum of thanksgiving was celebrated for God’s care for our nation and our country, attended also by His Excellency Mr. Cătălin Radu Dancu, Consul General of Romania in New York, together with the delegation of the Consulate in the American metropolis. At the same time, the national flags of Romania and of the United States of America were blessed, as a sign of our identity and belonging. The faithful, present in great numbers on this day honoring the Centennial of Romania and holding the flag of Romania in their hands, gave thanks to God for all His benefactions. Besides Fr. Michael Marcantoni, parish priest of the Greek church in Rochester, NY, faithful of the Ukrainian and Macedonian communities were also invited to the church’s celebration.

In honor of the Centennial of Greater Romania, four exhibitions were prepared in the church’s social hall, bearing witness through their exhibits to our country, its traditions and the beauty of the Romanian people:

  • The “Prof. Charles Carlton” PARISH MUSEUM was displayed in all its richness, presenting visitors with over 300 items of wood, ceramics and metal, as well as albums of traditional Romanian weavings and wood carvings. The collection of folk costumes was also at the center of attention. Most of the museum collection was donated to the church in Rochester by Charles Carlton, the respected professor of Romance languages at the University of Rochester. A lover of Romanian culture and art, Professor Carlton gathered many rare and extremely valuable objects during his frequent visits to Romania, which, upon his repose in the Lord in 2008, he left by will to our church, where he attended the Divine Liturgy every Sunday.
  • The opening of the EXHIBITION OF PHOTOGRAPHS AND DOCUMENTS OF THE TIME: the First World War, the personalities involved in this historic event, and copies of the documents of the Union of Bessarabia, Bukovina and Transylvania with the Motherland. This exhibition could be presented with the blessing of His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel and was prepared by the staff of the Library of the Holy Synod in Bucharest. The faces of the makers of the Great Union, full of light and fulfillment, in the photographs on display brought many tears to the eyes of those present. It was a gift from God that the images of Samoilă Mârza, the photographer of the Great Union, should also reach Rochester, the city of the “image,” as it is also called, since the first camera and the first TV image appeared here, and the headquarters of the Eastman Kodak company and of the Xerox Corporation are also located here.
  • Another exhibition that received much praise was “THE STRUGGLE OF THE ROMANIAN PEOPLE FOR NATIONAL UNITY AND INDEPENDENCE REFLECTED IN THE FINE ARTS”. Miniatures from the “Cronicon pictum Vindobonense,” paintings by Nicolae Grigorescu, Theodor Aman, Ștefan Luchian, D. Stoica, Barbu Iscovescu and Carol Popp de Szathmary, and images of sculptures by Constantin Brâncuși, Ion Vlasiu, Ion Georgescu and Gheorghe D. Anghel, accompanied by verses of the poets Mihai Eminescu, Vasile Alecsandri and George Coșbuc, who “sang” the Romanian people’s struggle for independence, drew the amazed gaze of those present, Romanians and Americans alike.
  • On this occasion there was also a display of the POSTERS of our parish school’s educational project “DE UNDE SUNT”. The enrolled young people proudly presented their projects before those present: His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, Consul General Cătălin Dancu, Very Rev. Fr. Daniel Ene, and many of the faithful. Applause and much joy accompanied the words and images of the posters presented. The aim of this educational project of the Metropolia, also carried out in our parish, was for young people to learn actively about their Romanian origin and then make their ancestral origin known to all, through respect for those who came before them. On a three-part poster board, the young people drew up a family tree going back to their grandparents, with their mother and her parents and their father and his parents, the age and place of birth of each, all accompanied by photographs. The second part of the presentation was choosing a tourist attraction, a personality or something unique from the area where one of their parents or grandparents was born, and presenting it. All participants rose to the occasion and received first place from the committee.

The day ended with a traditional Romanian meal in the church courtyard, during which a SPECIAL PROGRAM OF ROMANIAN FOLK DANCES was also presented by former members of the “Ciprian Porumbescu” Professional Ensemble of Suceava. His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae thanked everyone for preparing this event and then presented diplomas to our church’s prizewinners at the 2018 Religion Olympiad, Metropolia stage: first prize in the 13-18 age group to Miss Sofia Niculescu and third prize in the 8-12 age group to Maria Niculescu.

Through all of this, the day of June 3, 2018, held under the motto “1918-2018 Celebrating together!”, was an occasion to honor those who gave us the possibility to speak and feel Romanian and to be free, and also to share with our American friends and acquaintances the faith, the traditions and the beauty of our people and of our country, ROMANIA.

The American vision has changed over time, from “melting pot” to “salad bowl.” Our celebration sought to offer Americans the chance to meet the heroes of the Romanian people, creators and defenders of the values of the Romanian nation. Everyone’s feeling after this blessed day was that, even here, far away, having physically left Romania, we can keep its richness and its memory in our souls. For a few hours we rejoiced together, proud to be Romanians!

Reported by
Dean Fr. Daniel Ene

title: Divine Liturgy in Romanian in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Meeting with the Secretary of State for Religious Affairs of the Argentine Government.
intro:
The fourth stop on the pastoral itinerary of Dean Fr. Daniel Ene in South America, from March 2-8, 2018, was the old “El Dorado” of Latin America, Argentina. Argentina has traditionally been an important destination of Romanian emigration on the South American continent. The emigration of Romanians to Argentina began at the end of the 19th century and intensified in the first part of the 20th century, especially in the interwar period, during and immediately after the end of the Second World War. The emigrants from Romania had diverse ethnic origins: Jewish, German, Hungarian, Slovak, etc., and were drawn by the prospects of quick material success that the new host country could offer, as well as by the potential of exploring new geographic areas. Among them was Iulius Popper, an engineer and explorer from Romania (born in Bucharest in 1857), who arrived in Argentina in 1885 and made important contributions to the mapping and exploration of Tierra del Fuego. Toward the end of the interwar period, as well as during the Second World War and in the context created by the establishment of the communist regime in Romania, emigration took on a predominantly political character. Most of those who settled in Argentina during that period sought refuge from the horrors of war and the persecutions of the fascist and communist regimes that affected most of the European continent in the fifth decade of the last century.

The migration of Romanians to Argentina continued during the communist period in Romania, but at much lower levels, most of the emigrants also being political refugees.

After the Revolution of December 1989 and the restoration of democracy in our country, a small migration of Romanian citizens to Argentina was recorded. The census organized by the Argentine authorities in 2001 recorded 2,321 people born on the territory of Romania, of whom about half (1,212 people) lived in the capital, Buenos Aires. The census did not take into account the descendants of people born in Romania who currently hold Argentine citizenship. According to official data provided by the National Directorate of Migration of Argentina, between 2004 and 2012 a number of 70 Romanian citizens established permanent residence in Argentina, in addition to 31 Romanian citizens who obtained temporary residence over the same period.

Over time, several organizations of the Romanian community have operated in Buenos Aires, among which we mention the “Romanian Union” Circle, also known as the “Romanian Association for Mutual Assistance,” which was active from 1931 to 1974. Between 1981 and 1989 there was the “Mihai Eminescu” Association.

Currently, two Romanian associations operate in the Argentine capital: the Romania–Argentina Mutual Association (AS.ROM.AR), founded in 2000, whose aim is to promote Romanian culture and traditions as well as ties with the homeland, and the Romanian Orthodox Christian Association of Argentina (ACORA), founded in 2003, which was involved in the registration of the Romanian Orthodox Church in Argentina and also takes care of the Romanian “Saint Andrew” mission in Buenos Aires. This mission began its activity on December 14, 2008, when the Romanian Orthodox faithful of Buenos Aires, Argentina, experienced great joy: the first Divine Liturgy celebrated by Iconom Stavrofor Fr. Vasile-Ioan Tivadar, appointed parish priest of the newly established Mission by His Eminence Archbishop Nicolae. Since 2009, the mission has had no priest, and the Romanian community has dispersed among the other Orthodox churches in Argentina, the Greek or the Antiochian church.

It was in the context of these realities that Fr. Daniel Ene began his visit, at the invitation of Her Excellency Carmen-Liliana PODGOREAN, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Romania to the Argentine Republic. The first stop of the visit was on Saturday, March 3, 2018, at the National Basilica of the Virgin Mary of Luján, patroness of Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Luján is the most important Catholic pilgrimage site in South America and has an adjoining Marian Museum which gathers, in the spaces next to the church, images of the Mother of God from all corners of the world. Here there is also an Orthodox icon of the Mother of God covered in silver, given by His Beatitude Patriarch Teoctist, Patriarch of Romania, to the church of Luján and to the Romanian community of Argentina in 2003. On the feast of the Annunciation, March 25, 2003, the icon was placed at the specially prepared altar in the Marian museum by His Eminence Archbishop Kirilos Doumat, Archbishop of the Antiochian Orthodox Church, together with His Excellency Monsignor Ruben de Monte, Archbishop of Mercedes-Luján. The procession with the icon from Romania was attended by His Excellency the Ambassador of Romania to Argentina at that time, Mr. Victor Micula, Mr. Constantin Petre, Consul General of Romania in Buenos Aires, and Mr. Sergiu Ionescu, president of the Orthodox Christian Association of Argentina. The icon is still in the Museum, although in a different place than the original one, alongside images of the Mother of God from Greece and Serbia. Fr. Daniel Ene visited the Romanian altar in Luján together with Ambassador Carmen Podgorean, Mrs. Gabriela Enache, Consul General of Romania in Buenos Aires, and Mr. Mircea Borza, Economic Consul of Romania in Argentina. With the permission of the Catholic authorities, Fr. Daniel offered an Akathist prayer dedicated to the Mother of God.

The next day, Sunday, March 4, the Romanian community of Buenos Aires took part in the Divine Liturgy in Romanian, celebrated for the first time in more than 9 years by Dean Fr. Daniel Ene at the “Dormition of the Mother of God” Greek Orthodox Cathedral in Buenos Aires, together with His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Tarasios of the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Buenos Aires and South America. On the same day, Fr. Daniel officiated a Te Deum service at the Embassy of Romania, with the blessing of the National Flag and a commemoration of the Heroes who contributed to the achievement of the Great Union, whose Centennial is being celebrated this year. After the service, the Romanian community present took part in a series of discussions about the future of the Romanian community in Argentina and the need for a Romanian priest at the Saint Andrew mission in Buenos Aires. The discussions were also attended by Mr. Sergiu Ionescu, who is president of ACORA as well as president of the parish council of the Romanian church. Fr. Daniel thanked him for his care in keeping alive the Romanian Orthodox Christian association and the Saint Andrew Chapel in Buenos Aires, assuring him that in the future there will be a more active pastoral presence of the Metropolia in Argentina. Both in his homily after the Divine Liturgy and during this meeting, Fr. Daniel urged the Romanian community to preserve its spiritual identity and to use the Romanian language as an occasion for unity. “The Romanian language expresses the culture, the values and the richness of our traditions, and unites in one great spiritual community all those who speak it, regardless of where they live,” Fr. Daniel told those present. He also encouraged Romanians to teach their children the Romanian language and to urge them not only to know but also to love their Orthodox faith and their mother tongue. In this context, Fr. Daniel praised the fact that the Faculty of Law of the University of Buenos Aires has a Romanian language department, with four levels of study, currently held by Sergiu Ionescu, president of ACORA, and thanked Ambassador Carmen Podgorean for her exemplary zeal and dedication in promoting authentic Romanian culture in the vast Argentine cultural space.

It should be emphasized that the program of the Embassy of Romania in Argentina is worthy of the place where it is located. The Romanian proverb “The right person in the right place” is fulfilled in the arrangement of Romania’s diplomatic corps in Buenos Aires and Argentina. The cultural refinement and sociological training of the Ambassador could only make her the perfect choice for the position of Romania’s ambassador in the deeply cultural setting of the “Paris of Latin America,” Buenos Aires.

On Monday, March 5, Fr. Daniel Ene met with His Eminence Metropolitan Siluan, Antiochian Orthodox Archbishop of Buenos Aires and Argentina. Consul Mircea Borza also attended the meeting. His Eminence Siluan told Fr. Daniel that the Antiochian church enjoys the support and participation of the Romanian faithful in Argentina and assured him of His Eminence’s full help in caring for the Romanian faithful.

In the context of his visit to Argentina, Fr. Daniel Ene, accompanied by the Ambassador of Romania, Carmen Podgorean, and by Consul General Gabriela Enache, was received in audience on Tuesday, March 6, 2018, by the Secretary for Religious Affairs of the Argentine Republic, Ambassador Santiago M. de Estrada, accompanied by the General Coordinator for Religious Affairs, Ambassador Claudia E. Russo Bernagozzi. The visit to Argentina ended on Friday, March 8, 2018, after a brief one-day visit to Montevideo, Uruguay.

Fr. Daniel Ene

title: The First Visit of a Romanian Orthodox Priest to the “Bucharest” of Latin America – Montevideo, Uruguay
intro:
At the invitation of His Excellency Mr. Valentin FLOREA, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Romania to the Oriental Republic of Uruguay, Fr. Daniel Ene met on March 7, 2018 with the very small Romanian community of Montevideo. It was the first visit of a Romanian Orthodox priest to the capital of Uruguay. At the ambassador’s request, Fr. Daniel performed the blessing of the premises of the Embassy of Romania and of the ambassador’s residence.

Around noon, Dean Fr. Daniel Ene met with Fr. Ioannis Kriaris, parish priest of Saint Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church in Montevideo. They discussed the Orthodox community of Uruguay, which is not very large, and Fr. Ioannis’s contact with the Romanian community, which numbers a few dozen people. Fr. Ioannis assured Fr. Daniel of his support in the pastoral care of the Romanian faithful in Uruguay, offering the Romanian community the facilities of the Hellenic community for religious, social or cultural activities free of charge.

As this is the Centennial year of Greater Romania, the Embassy of Romania in Uruguay also organized a Te Deum service on the afternoon of March 7, celebrated by Fr. Daniel Ene. It took place beside the statue of Tudor Vladimirescu, which stands at the intersection of two major boulevards on the bank of the Río de la Plata, the “River of Silver,” the widest river or estuary in the world. The service glorifying God was followed with piety and wonder by the crowd of passersby in the area that afternoon. Besides Fr. Ioannis Kriaris, Ambassador Valentin Florea also took part in the Te Deum and the laying of flowers. On the same occasion, the bust of Tudor Vladimirescu was blessed. Fr. Daniel told those present: “The Te Deum, this church hymn in psalms, is a prayer of thanksgiving for the benefits bestowed upon the Romanian people, and also a fervent prayer to the Lord to care for the few Romanians here in Uruguay. We chose the statue of Tudor Vladimirescu as the place for this Te Deum because his struggle was a struggle for the unity and national integrity of the Romanian people.”

Assuring the ambassador of the support of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, Fr. Daniel also conveyed the prayer of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae for the diplomatic corps and the Romanians of Uruguay. This day and a half spent in the “Bucharest” of Latin America, as Montevideo is called among the Romanian community because of its countless urban similarities, was an occasion to show His Eminence’s real care not only for the large Romanian communities but also for the few who live here, in faraway Uruguay.

Fr. Daniel Ene

title: Cooperation Agreement Between the Faculty of Orthodox Theology in Sibiu and Saint Vladimir’s Orthodox Theological Seminary in New York
intro:
The “Saint Andrei Șaguna” Faculty of Orthodox Theology in Sibiu and Saint Vladimir’s Orthodox Theological Seminary in New York signed an academic cooperation agreement on Monday, June 25. Faculty and students of the two institutions will benefit from programs, scholarships and joint projects.

The agreement was signed in Sibiu, at the Faculty of Orthodox Theology, in the presence of the heads of the two theological schools, the president of Saint Vladimir’s Seminary, Very Rev. Prof. Dr. Chad Hatfield, and the dean of the Șaguna academy, Rev. Prof. Dr. Nicolae Chifăr. Also present at the signing was His Eminence Laurențiu, Archbishop of Sibiu and Metropolitan of Transylvania, who blessed this agreement between the two institutions, a particularly important moment for the theological community of Sibiu. Faculty members of the Faculty of Theology in Sibiu and theology students were present as well.

In his address, Fr. Nicolae Chifăr stressed the importance of this moment for the faculty in Sibiu.

“This cooperation means exchanges of professors who will give lectures and papers at our faculty and at Saint Vladimir’s Seminary in New York. The partnership also provides for research stays for students, especially master’s and doctoral students, both shorter and longer ones, with a scholarship offered by the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, on condition that at the end of the research stay the students remain for a period of time and serve within this Metropolia. This scholarship bears the name of Fr. Dumitru Stăniloae,” the dean said.

For his part, Fr. Chad Hatfield spoke about the help the institution he leads receives by signing this cooperation agreement with a prestigious faculty in Romania.

“It is important for us to understand that signing this agreement is only a beginning, and with God’s help we believe this agreement will develop and change according to needs. It is very important for us, who study theology as a minority in various cultures, to have strong ties with the Faculties of Theology in the mother countries, where Orthodoxy is deeply rooted in the culture. In America, Orthodox Christians make up 1 percent of the population, and in this context Saint Vladimir’s Seminary has been a missionary school; it has always been at the forefront in training apologists, and the same has been true of the help it has given to the liturgical life of the Church,” Fr. Chad Hatfield emphasized.

The Șaguna Cross for Fr. Chad Hatfield

His Eminence Metropolitan Laurențiu thanked the guest for his openness toward the Romanian theological community and for the support he has given to Romanian theologians and to our Church. As a sign of appreciation, the hierarch presented him with the “Șaguna Cross for Priests” distinction and invited him to come to Sibiu more often.

“Thank you for returning to Sibiu with what we agreed on a year ago for our theological schools. I came to know your seminary on a visit to New York, but above all while preparing my doctorate, when I drew a great deal on the theology of the great professors there, professors who left fundamental works of theology. Fr. Alexander Schmemann influenced me so much that I have given a great many lectures on the liturgical theology of this great theologian,” the hierarch said.

Fr. Chad Hatfield presented a number of books published in English by professors of Saint Vladimir’s Orthodox Theological Seminary in New York. Fr. Nicolae Chifăr, in turn, presented the guest with the latest theological publications from Sibiu.

title: Orthodox Brotherly Communion in Chicago
intro:
The participation of His Eminence Archbishop Irineu of Alba Iulia in the proceedings of the 82nd Congress of the Romanian Orthodox Archdiocese of the United States of America brought much joy to the priests, the Congress delegates and the faithful of SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago.

The days of the Congress proceedings were followed by days of pilgrimage to the Orthodox monasteries and churches of the Chicago metropolitan area. The first stop was the Serbian Orthodox Cathedral of the Holy Resurrection, not far from the Metropolitan Center. His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, His Eminence Archbishop Irineu, Archdeacon Rafael, who accompanied Archbishop Irineu, and Deacon Aurel of the Metropolitan Center were welcomed by the clergy of the Cathedral. The guests heard the history of the Serbian Cathedral and had the opportunity to venerate the relics of Saint Sebastian of Jackson and California, the first Orthodox priest ordained on American soil, in 1892, who once served at this Cathedral.

The pilgrimage continued with a visit to the Serbian Monastery of Saint Sava in Libertyville, IL, founded by Saint Mardarije of Libertyville and Chicago, which also houses the Saint Sava Seminary of the Serbian Diocese. The guests venerated the relics of the monastery’s founder, placed for veneration last year, 2017, with the local proclamation of Saint Mardarije’s glorification. A memorial prayer was said at the grave of Metropolitan Christopher near the church.

The Serbian Monastery of New Gracanica in Third Lake, IL, the seat of the Serbian Orthodox Diocese of the Central USA, was the pilgrims’ next stop. They visited the monastery church, the diocesan headquarters and its property, which covers more than 50 hectares.

Lunchtime was spent at the Greek women’s monastery of Saint John Chrysostom in Pleasant Prairie, WI. Here they visited the chapel and the large church of the monastery, and the guests were told about the history and spiritual life of the monastery, which is under the obedience of Elder Ephraim of Arizona.

The last stop of the day was a visit to the Russian Orthodox Cathedral and the headquarters of the Russian Diocese outside Russia for the Central USA (ROCOR). Metropolitan Nicolae and Archbishop Irineu were received by Fr. Andrei, on behalf of His Eminence Archbishop Peter, who spoke to them about the history of the Russian Orthodox presence in North America.

The second day of the program offered to the Romanian delegation included a stop at the University of Chicago. They visited the Divinity School, where the well-known Romanian historian Mircea Eliade taught in the mid-1980s. The delegation stopped for a few minutes in the lecture hall where Prof. Mircea Eliade lectured, and then went to the nearby Oak Woods Cemetery, where he is buried alongside his wife, Mrs. Christinel Eliade. Here, Archbishop Irineu, together with Metropolitan Nicolae and the other members of the delegation, prayed for the repose of the souls of the servants of God Mircea and Christinel.

The Greek Cathedral of the Annunciation in the center of the city, along with landmark sights of Chicago, concluded the visit of the delegation from Alba Iulia. At the end of their time in Chicago, Archbishop Irineu expressed his appreciation for the good organization and his thanks for the special welcome from the Romanian Orthodox community of Chicago on the occasion of the Archdiocese Congress.

title: Message of His Beatitude DANIEL, Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church, on the Sunday of Romanian Migrants
intro:
Unity of faith and unity of nation in the Centenary Year

The first Sunday after the feast of the Dormition of the Mother of God was dedicated by the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church, at its working session of February 25-26, 2009, to all Romanian migrants. This Sunday is a good occasion to address a word of blessing and spiritual encouragement to the Romanian Orthodox faithful who have settled or are working temporarily abroad.

By cultivating the awareness of the unity of faith and nation, the Romanian Orthodox Church contributed to the preparation of the great historical events aimed at the national unity of the Romanians, namely: the Union of the Principalities (1859), the State Independence of Romania (1877-1878) and the Great Union (1918), which was decisive for the formation of the unitary national state of Romania.

The Great Union of December 1, 1918 had positive consequences for the new, reunited Romanian state and for the Romanian Orthodox Church. On December 18/31, 1919, the Bishop of Caransebeș, Miron Cristea, was elected to the vacant see of Metropolitan Primate of Romania, and in 1925 he became the first Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church, followed by the process of the unified organization of the Church throughout Romania.

On October 15, 1922, in a ceremony held at the Cathedral of the Reunification of the Nation in Alba Iulia, King Ferdinand I and Queen Marie were crowned as sovereigns of Greater Romania, an act that symbolized the union of all Romanians “from the Dniester to the Tisza” under the same scepter.

In the last decade, the spiritual needs of the Romanians living far from the Homeland have led the Romanian Orthodox Church to make a pastoral priority of strengthening the Romanian communities around the country’s borders and in the Romanian diaspora, a new reality that has reached a scale never before seen in the history of the Romanian people. In this regard, the Romanian Patriarchate has cultivated the unity and identity of Romanians through the establishment of dioceses, deaneries and parishes, as well as through social, educational and cultural programs meant to respond concretely to the requests coming from the faithful. At the same time, through the liturgical and pastoral-social activity of the Romanian Orthodox hierarchs and clergy abroad, the Romanian Orthodox Church strives to build, together with the church in the soul, places of worship wherever there are Romanian communities, thus giving every Romanian Orthodox Christian living abroad the opportunity to hear the holy services in his mother tongue and to go to confession and receive Holy Communion in a Romanian church, thereby keeping the bond with the Mother Church in the Homeland. The Romanian Patriarchate also helps these Romanian communities financially, according to its means, either directly or through the necessary steps and recommendations to the State Secretariat for Religious Affairs and the Ministry for Romanians Abroad. In this context, on July 17, 2018, the Protocol of Cooperation between the Romanian Patriarchate and the Ministry for Romanians Abroad was signed at the Patriarchal Palace. This protocol provides for a series of projects, programs and actions aimed at supporting the Romanian communities beyond the country’s borders in preserving their ethnic, cultural and religious identity. The joint efforts for the benefit of Romanian communities everywhere concern the construction, repair, conservation and furnishing of churches, libraries and museums, and the renovation and upkeep of memorial houses, historical monuments and cemeteries. In addition, there are plans to organize traditional events on the occasion of the great feasts, various cultural events, camps for children and young people from beyond the country’s borders, Romanian language competitions held as part of the Sunday School project, and religion classes aimed at familiarizing children with the Orthodox faith, with the connection between the Christian faith and Romanian culture, and with respect for religious freedom.

In particular, the liturgical services broadcast daily by Radio TRINITAS and TRINITAS Television of the Romanian Patriarchate are of real spiritual benefit to the Orthodox Romanians living temporarily or permanently far from the Homeland. 

The year 2018, the Centenary Year dedicated to the Makers of the Great Union of 1918, is in a special way a year of gratitude and of Romanian communion, and at the same time a blessed occasion to work more intensely to cultivate the unity of the apostolic faith received from the Holy Apostle Andrew, the First-Called, Protector of Romania, who is also the patron of the new National Cathedral.

By the mercy of God, through the prayers of the Mother of God, of the Holy Apostle Andrew, Protector of Romania, and of all the saints, and through the generosity of the clergy and faithful of the Romanian Patriarchate in the country and abroad, as well as of the Government of Romania, the Bucharest City Hall, other city halls and some county councils in Romania, on November 25, 2018, the National Cathedral will be consecrated, this new edifice being a practical liturgical necessity and also a symbol of Romanian spirituality. The People’s Salvation Cathedral or the National Cathedral, whose main patronal feasts are the Ascension of the Lord and Heroes’ Day, symbolically unites the love for God of a Christian, self-sacrificing and generous people with the gratitude we permanently owe to the Heroes of the Nation.

We also take this opportunity to thank the hierarchs, clergy and faithful of the Romanian diaspora who, like many founders of churches and monasteries, have supported, together with the Orthodox Romanians in the Homeland, the continuation and completion of all the works on the National Cathedral, thus experiencing the joy of being themselves “a lineage of voivodes”, Christ-loving Romanians, founders of the Church and of the Nation.

We pray to the Merciful God to grant all Romanians living among foreigners health and salvation, peace and happiness, together with the joy of always keeping their Orthodox faith, their national unity and their Romanian spirituality!

With appreciation and fatherly blessing,

† DANIEL
Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church

title: Celebration of the Great Union in Sacramento
intro:
The Romanians of Sacramento, at the encouragement of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas and in the presence of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, invite you to take part in the celebration of the Centenary of the Great Union of 1918.

The guests of honor will be Academician Ioan Aurel Pop, President of the Romanian Academy and Rector of Babeș-Bolyai University in Cluj, historian Sebastian Doreanu of Denver, CO, and philosopher Octavian Gabor of Peoria, IL.

The celebration will take place at the Clubhouse Hall at Carmichael Park, 5750 Grant Avenue, Sacramento, CA, 95608, on Monday, September 3, 2018, from 2:30 to 5:30 pm. An exhibition of historical photographs and patriotic songs will complement the presentations.

title: Religious Camp for the Children of Saint Nicholas Parish, New York
intro:
St. Nicholas Church in New York organized a summer camp from August 22 to 26, 2018 at St. Dimitrios the New Monastery in Middletown, NY for children aged 7 to 14. Eighteen children took part.

The camp was religious, educational and recreational in character. Over the five days, the children discovered themselves and found themselves in Christ and in the Church. The activities they took part in and the friendships they formed with one another showed that Orthodoxy is lived (and alive). They had the joy of being together with friends, of learning truths that will shape their behavior at home and in society, and of being in communion with others, a communion that helps them draw closer to Christ.

The program was varied: every morning and evening the children took part in prayer. During the day they were involved in various sports games, contests, hands-on workshops, themed catechetical talks given by the fathers of the monastery, music and folk dance lessons, striking the toaca, and Christian riddles. Added to these was a Romanian evening with traditional food, games, songs and a campfire. Two evenings featured educational films followed by discussion. Each child received a prayer rope and was introduced to the Prayer of the Heart. They also drew the Holy Cross with the initials ICXC/NIKA on a piece of wood. On Sunday, all the children attended the Divine Liturgy and sang the responses at the chanters’ stand. The true spiritual treasure of the camp was that all the children received the Body and Blood of Christ.

We thank everyone who made this wonderful five-day experience possible: volunteers, organizers, parents and children. I had the chance to meet people devoted to God and to the community. For me, this camp was like a return to childhood.

We give thanks to Fr. Vincențiu and Monk Serafim for the hospitality, help and love they offered us, which made it possible to organize this camp for the benefit of the children and the community. Thanks also to Mrs. Florica Radu, the camp’s main coordinator; to Mr. Leonard Milea for the history, geography and music lessons; to Mr. Ciprian Mureșan for every dish, prepared with much love and exceptionally tasty; and, last but not least, to Danielle Radu for the patience, love and responsibility with which she cared for the children.

The joy of meeting at the camp was doubled this year by the celebration of the Centennial of the Great Union, a significant landmark of love, faith and unity for each of us. On this occasion the children danced the Hora Unirii and sang patriotic songs.

This camp comes as a crowning of faith in God, because cultivating a bond between Church, School and Family is essential to an authentic education for life. With the help of the Good God, we hope to meet again next year.

Alexandra Mureșan

title: Patronal Feast of Saints Joachim and Anna Parish in Seattle, Washington
intro:
“This is the day the Lord has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it,” under the protection of Saints Joachim and Anna. Because for several days the Lord has given us the gift of joy, peace of soul and spiritual gladness, I believe this is the most fitting motto to reflect the state of us, the faithful who took part in the events connected with the holy feast. Already on the eve, several of the faithful of our church came in the evening to offer praise and spiritual hymns to the Holy Virgin Mary.

On the morning of the feast of the Nativity of the Mother of God, the Divine Liturgy was celebrated, and then, at the time for the homily from the ambo, with the blessing of the serving priest, one of the altar boys read the homily so that it might reach even more deeply into the minds and hearts of the English-speaking children and young people present at the holy service.

After the dismissal, a new sound began to ring out in the church, beautiful and harmonious, as if it had come down from the slender, tall bell towers of the monasteries of northern Bukovina… Little children born here in America, who perhaps had never seen or heard a semantron before, struck it with such enthusiasm and eagerness, fascinated by its sound, as if calling the people of God and at the same time announcing to them the beginning of the yearly celebration of our holy patrons.

We gathered again at the hour of Vespers, this time to honor the parents according to the flesh of the Mother of God. On the very holy day of the commemoration of Saints Joachim and Anna, the faithful of the church, dressed in folk costumes, adorned it like living icons, “icons” that were a true delight to behold. Communion with the All-Holy Body and Blood of our most precious Savior; the veneration of the holy relics of Saint Anna; the joy of meeting again with our Romanian brothers and sisters from all the historical regions of the motherland, as well as the fellowship with American and Greek guests and with pilgrims who came from Canada .., these will remain as unfading memories.

Although His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was unable to attend the patronal feast of the church this year, he sent us a message of congratulation and blessing, thus showing the fatherly care he has for us. In his heartfelt message, our Hierarch told us that “the feast of the Holy Parents Joachim and Anna is the feast of joy and of hope. For the Nativity of the Virgin Mary from her parents Joachim and Anna, after much persistent prayer and steadfast faith, brought joy to the whole world, as the troparion of the feast of the Nativity of the Mother of God tells us. The Nativity of the Virgin Mary brought joy not only to the family of Joachim and Anna, who had long awaited a child as a sign of heavenly blessing, but to all mankind, for it was the sign that God had not forgotten His creation and, through the birth of Mary, was beginning His plan for the salvation of man. It is also the feast of hope, for our persistent prayers to God are heard, and God’s answer can go far beyond what we ask. The child, asked for by the righteous Joachim and Anna as a blessing for their family, was the one who carried the Savior in her womb and gave Him to the world.”

The atmosphere of peace, joy and brotherly love continued at the agape meal in the church hall. In such holy moments, all you can do is exclaim: “How good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together!” And that is because it was very hard for us to part from one another at the end of the holy day. It felt as though the Liturgy had not ended; it continued through the service at the brotherly agape meal and especially toward evening, when a group of faithful went to visit one of the sisters of our community who is in grave suffering, and to comfort her little children, who care for her in an exemplary way.

The feast of our holy patrons has not ended. It continues in our souls, celebrating as in a spiritual feast, since in our hearts burns the lampada lit on the eve of the feast! We will keep it burning with the oil of persistent prayer and will remember with great love the wonderful moments the Lord has given us!

Oh, if only the nations knew our joys, our uplifting moments! I believe they would all run, young and old, to the doors of our Orthodox Church, to taste at least a little and to share in our undying joys.

I will try to end my report here from Seattle with a poem written by someone inspired by the spiritual beauty of this special event in the life of our parish:

Our beloved faithful,
Seeing you so beautiful,
Dressed as in days of old,
.. Like our forefathers:
From our most beloved country,

… And when I look upon these children…
Adorned in holy embroidered blouses,
I seem to glimpse icons… saints …
Living Icons: children… parents …!!!

- You are … ! you are the future!
- Of Orthodoxy! - You, the people!!!
You will carry on, I know…
The holy faith… In Seattle … …!!!

I look at you, dear Transylvanians,
At our precious brothers .. from Bessarabia ..,
And at the Romanians from the Old Kingdom
All of you: the same dough!!

When I behold you from the holy Altar,
Enfolded in grace,
I can do nothing but give thanks,
To the Good Father, the Heavenly One!

This costume, called a folk costume…,
Received as a gift from our forefathers,
When I gladly look on others,
And see that they too are adorned …,

With such adornment and garment!
Which shows me a holy person!!
- Look at yourselves! - We are beautiful!!!
And what FAITH we have!!!

See here .. a living Icon…
A small.., holy Romania …!!!
How beautiful, oh, how beautiful,
All of us here, in Christ!!!
All of us living in Christ!!!

Carrying in our souls a treasure..
Is it too little to say .. A rare flower…?!
The holy faith of our forefathers,
And the sweet Romanian speech …!!!

Here, far away, ambassadors,
Carrying in our souls as treasures…,
Tradition, as a treasure,
The holy faith, a rare flower!

Living here so intensely
With our longing, a longing .. immense …
Our bitterness is sweetened
As we celebrate.. the Centennial …!

… With such treasures, I cannot perish,
Christians, I live as in Heaven;
For all that is holy and Romanian,
Here… Far away… , I live …!!!

I humbly urge you all,
Love, beloved ones, the faith
And our ancestral law
And the Romanian custom …

Protosyngellos Andrei Aioanei
