title: Call to Take Part in the Referendum of October 6-7, 2018
intro:
September 21, 2018

Reverend Fathers,

Beloved brothers and sisters in the Lord,

I address to you this fatherly call to take part in the Referendum held on October 6-7, 2018 to amend Article 48 of the Constitution of Romania. I remind you that we discussed this subject last year at the Deanery Assemblies of our Archdiocese in the United States of America.

The proposed wording of Art. 48, para. 1 of the Constitution of Romania is the following: “The family is founded on the freely consented marriage between a man and a woman, on their equality and on the right and duty of parents to ensure the upbringing, education and instruction of their children.” The ambiguous wording “between spouses” is thus replaced with the specification “between a man and a woman”.

The family is the oldest and holiest institution known to humankind. In the Book of Genesis we discover the personal manner in which man was created: “God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them. Then God blessed them, saying: Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it” (Genesis 1, 26-28). It is made clear and reinforced through repetition that “God created man in His own image; male and female He created them”. From the beginning, man and woman were created for a communion of life and love. The fulfillment of the creation of man and woman was the blessing to be fruitful and multiply. The child is the fruit of the love between a man and a woman, and only this love brings forth life.

The proposed wording of Art. 48, para. 1 of the Constitution of Romania respects the family as God created it and offers the chance to defend the future of our children and families. To this end, 14 states in Europe have adopted constitutional provisions by which marriage is explicitly recognized as the freely consented union between a man and a woman. Through the vote of its citizens, Romania can join these states in defending the Christian values of Europe and the order of divine creation.

Romanian citizens in America (faithful of our parishes, other Romanian Christians, all Romanians who care about the country in which they were born) must help defend the future of Romania by voting YES in the referendum.

I therefore urge all of you, priests and faithful, to take part in the referendum held at the Consulates of Romania and other polling stations, to explain the importance of this vote to the fellow Romanians you meet, and to urge them as well to vote YES.

We pray that the Lord may bless us and strengthen us all in this desire to defend our future on earth and our salvation in heaven!

† Metropolitan Nicolae
of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas

title: Celebrating the Centennial of Greater Romania in Upland, California
intro:
The church year began in the Exaltation of the Holy Cross parish in Upland, California, with an abundance of blessings and spiritual joy. Two years after the consecration of our church, in this year of the Centennial of the Great Union of 1918, God, Who is wondrous in His saints, ordained three days of special feast.

On September 14, when the Romanian Orthodox Church of Upland celebrates its patronal feast, the faithful of the parish rejoiced at the visit of the Eparchial Secretary, Fr. Daniel Ene, who brought with him on his pilgrimage to the Exaltation of the Holy Cross parish the relics of Saint Anna, the mother of the Mother of God, and of Saint Empress Theodora of Byzantium. Through his kindness, for three days the faithful of the parish prayed to these two holy mothers of the right-believing Church and praised God in Trinity.

On Friday morning, September 14, Archimandrite Nicodim together with Fr. Daniel celebrated the Divine Liturgy of the glorious Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross. That same evening, a group of priests performed the sacrament of Holy Unction, attended by a large number of faithful. They were anointed with blessed oil and also received a blessing from the holy relics of Saints Anna and Theodora.

The liturgical program continued on Saturday, September 15, at midday, with the Akathist of the Holy Cross, followed by the Canon of Saint Anna, the Te Deum service for the blessing of the Romanian flag, and Fr. Daniel’s homily on the symbolism of the Romanian banner. Saturday evening Vespers gave a good start to the last day of the weekend, the Sunday after the Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

The joy of the feast also filled Sunday, September 16, when a large number of faithful attended the Divine Liturgy, received the Body and Blood of the Lord, and offered their tribute of veneration to the holy relics, which pour out blessings over this place of Romanian Orthodoxy. At the end of the Divine Liturgy, Fr. Ene blessed the children with a prayer for the beginning of the school year.

In his homily, Fr. Ene emphasized the importance of this centennial year in the history of the Romanians, listing all the events leading up to the Great Union at Alba-Iulia, as well as the context of its fulfillment, to the joy of the Romanians of the three principalities, Wallachia, Moldavia and Transylvania. His words were accompanied by a large number of photographs of the official documents of the Great Union and of the historic moments of 100 years ago. The documentary material was displayed in the social hall. All the faithful took part in the festive meal of our church and were able to browse through these pages of history.

The three feast days of our church concluded with the singing of La Mulți Ani in honor of our country, Romania, and of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross parish on its anniversary.                       

Deacon Valentin Despoiu

title: Appeal of the National Church Assembly for Participation in the Referendum of October 6-7, 2018
intro:
Let Us Say YES to the Family Blessed by God!

Appeal of the National Church Assembly for participation in the referendum of October 6-7, 2018 -*

1. The National Church Assembly, composed of all the hierarchs of the Holy Synod and the representatives of the clergy and of the lay faithful from the eparchies of the Romanian Patriarchate, gathered in its session of September 29, 2018, urges all Romanian Orthodox citizens to take part in the referendum and to say YES to clarifying the text of article 48 of the Constitution of Romania concerning the definition of marriage, that is, replacing the confusing expression “the freely consented union between spouses” with the clear and precise wording “the freely consented union between a man and a woman”.

2. Through this clear and unequivocal clarification in the Constitution of Romania, the family is affirmed, defended and promoted as the fundamental human institution created and blessed by God for the growth and continuation of humanity, according to the words of Holy Scripture: “So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them. Then God blessed them, and God said to them, ‘Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it.’” (Genesis 1, 27-28). This family, based on marriage between a man and a woman, was blessed and honored by the Savior Jesus Christ through His presence, together with His mother and His disciples, at the Wedding in Cana of Galilee, where He performed the miracle of turning water into wine (cf. John 2, 1-11), thus showing the holy value of the conjugal family for the life of the Church. In this sense, the Holy Apostle Paul recommends that the love of the bridegroom for the bride be like the love of Christ for the Church (cf. Ephesians 5, 22-25, 32).

3. The family blessed by God, for cultivating mutual love and giving birth to children, is a source of life for every people and for all humanity. Therefore, taking part in the referendum on October 6 and 7, 2018, is an act of confessing faith in God’s love for the family, an act of the utmost responsibility for the future of the Romanian people, and an examination of spiritual maturity in choosing between permanent values and ephemeral ideologies.

4. The word “referendum” means: “direct consultation of citizens called to express themselves by vote on a draft law of particular importance for the state or on issues of general interest” (DEX). Therefore, the participation of the state’s citizens in this decisive referendum on the definition of marriage in the Constitution of Romania is a profoundly democratic and national-patriotic act, of particular importance for the entire Romanian people, because the vote is for the defense of the family based on marriage between a man and a woman and for the future of the children of the Romanian people. In fact, article 2 of the Constitution of Romania states that national sovereignty of Romania is exercised through referendum.

5. In spite of many actions of aggressive boycott and unjust denigration of the referendum, we must defend the sacred gift of the life of the human person born of conjugal love between a man and a woman, thus also cherishing the generations of parents and children who have ensured the continuity of the Romanian people through the centuries.

Let us therefore honor the Centennial of the Great Union of 1918 through a great union of mind and national action in defense of the Christian family and of the future of the Romanian people!

President of the National Church Assembly

† DANIEL
Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church

* To be read in all churches on Sunday, September 30, 2018, and Monday, October 1, 2018.

title: Symposium Dedicated to the Centennial of the Great Union at Villanova University
intro:
On Saturday, October 20, 2018, from 10:30 am to 2:00 pm, a symposium dedicated to the Centennial of the Great Union was held at Villanova University, Dougherty Hall, in Villanova, PA. Entitled “MIRABILIS RESTITVTIO VNITATIS DACO-ROMANORVM. ANNO DOMINI MCMXVIII”, the symposium was organized by Holy Trinity Romanian Orthodox Parish of Philadelphia, at the initiative and under the high patronage of His Eminence Metropolitan Dr. NICOLAE CONDREA.

This cultural event set out to present, both to the American public and to the Romanians of the American diaspora, the immense efforts and sacrifices made by the Romanian people and the Romanian Orthodox Church to fulfill the centuries-old dream of the Romanians: the union of all Romanians in a single free and democratic state. The Romanian soldiers and officers who fought and gave their lives on the front in the First World War, together with the great personalities who waged fierce diplomatic battles, succeeded through their heroism in leaving us a whole country, and  in writing the year 1918 into the book of the nation as the “Annus Mirabilis”. The invited speakers set out to speak about the sacrifices of such personalities, lay and clerical, for the victory of the Romanians and the Union of Alba Iulia, and about how the Romanian press in the United States helped support the great national project of the Union of Bukovina, Bessarabia and Transylvania with the motherland.

We first had the joy of listening to His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, who gave an introductory address emphasizing the importance of celebrating the Centennial and the role of the Romanian Orthodox Church in bringing about the Great Union of 1918. His Eminence pointed out that by declaring 2018 the Homage Year of the unity of faith and nation and Commemorative Year of the founders of the Great Union, the Romanian Patriarchate encouraged the organization of cultural events throughout its jurisdiction,  meant to revive the memory of forgotten heroes of the Great Union who sacrificed themselves for its fulfillment.

Fr. Nicolai Buga, the organizer of the symposium, introduced the two guests who would lecture alongside him.

The first speaker was Prof. Mona Momescu, PhD in philology from the University of Bucharest, lecturer at the “N. Iorga” Chair of Romanian Language and Culture at Columbia University, New York, a program administered by the Romanian Language Institute and Columbia University. Prof. Momescu is a full professor at “Ovidius” University of Constanța. Among her publications we mention: Canon, identitate, tranziție, Ed. Univ București, 2008, Idolii forului (co-edited with Sorin Adam Matei), Corint, 2010, as well as theoretical articles in Romanian studies and on the history of Romanian language teaching in the USA, published in various academic journals. She has taken part in seminars and conferences on distance teaching of Romanian and in projects using various information technology applications in teaching the Romanian language.

Prof. Mona Momescu’s lecture was entitled Romanian Language, Culture and Traditions - Unity and Continuity of the Romanian Identity in the U.S. [Romanian Language, Culture and Traditions - Unity and Continuity in the United States]. After the Great Union of 1918, Romanians no longer emigrated to the USA in large groups. Still, they continued to come and to integrate into the old established communities. For them, as for all those who chose or were forced to live somewhere other than their own country, the Romanian language kept them united and at times helped them calm their fear and loneliness and ease their longing for home. Romanian was used in publications as well as in written, personal correspondence with the churches. Prof. Momescu’s presentation focused mainly on the ways in which the use of Romanian (in all its registers) and the birth of a Romanian-American vocabulary allowed these communities to preserve their identity and spread their culture and traditions.

Next came Fr. Prof. Dr. Theodor Damian, of Metropolitan College of New York, NY, where he teaches Philosophy and Ethics. Holder of an honorary doctorate (Doctor Honoris Causa) from Bioterra University of Bucharest, a doctorate in Theology from the University of Bucharest and another doctorate from Fordham University, Fr. Damian also teaches courses  at St. Vladimir’s Theological Seminary and at Spiru Haret University in Bucharest. He is also the parish priest of Saints Peter and Paul Church in Astoria, NY.

His lecture, entitled Nicolae V. Hodoroaba, Militant in the Fight for the Great Reunification of Transylvania with Romania [Fr. Nicolae V. Hodoroabă, Militant in the Fight for the Great Reunification of Transylvania with Romania], evoked the luminous figure of a professor at the Seminary of Iași, a true hero who in the First World War served the Romanian Army at the front as a military chaplain, an eyewitness to the sacrifices of the Romanian soldiers and officers who died for the return of Transylvania to the motherland.  

The third speaker was Fr. Prof. Nicolai Buga, parish priest of the host church. A former professor of the History of the Romanian Orthodox Church at the Orthodox Seminary in Bucharest, who also taught at the National School of Political and Administrative Studies in the same city and at Saint Tikhon’s Seminary in South Canaan, PA, Fr. Nicolai Buga has translated important theological books, such as: John Meyendorff, Hristos în gândirea creștină răsăriteană, translated from English, (Christ in the Eastern Christian Thought). București: IBMBOR, 1997;  Jaroslav Pelikan, Tradiţia creştină. O istorie a dezvoltării doctrinei, volume 2, Spiritul creștinismului răsăritean (600-1700), translated from English with notes by Fr. N. Buga [The Christian Tradition: A History of the Development of Christian Doctrine, vol. 2 The Spirit of Eastern Christendom (600-1700)], Iaşi: Polirom, 2006.

In his lecture, entitled Vasile Stoica and His Contribution to the Achievement and International recognition of the Greater Romania [Vasile Stoica and His Contribution to the Achievement and International Recognition of Greater Romania], Fr. Buga sought to bring back to our memory, in this year of the Centennial of the Great Union of 1918, the figure of an important  personality of our modern history: Vasile Stoica, a great scholar and diplomat, a  patriot to whom we largely owe the support the Romanian people enjoyed from American public opinion and officials at the end of the First World War, and the international recognition of the Union of Transylvania with Romania. Sadly, after the communist regime was installed, Vasile  Stoica was declared an “enemy of the people”, and for this “guilt” he was thrown into prison at Jilava, where he was left to die before his time, in 1959.

In conclusion, one could say that the theme of the symposium might be placed under the words of Nicolae Iorga: “Without a toll of suffering, without tears from the overflow of pain, without blood from the overflow of life, no nation is redeemed from bondage.”  It remains for us, today’s generation,  from the humblest peasant to the bishop, to learn to treasure this “toll of suffering” that made the Great Union possible.

Reported by Fr. Prof. Nicolai Buga

title: Celebration of the Centennial of Greater Romania in Seattle, WA
intro:
At this great event, feeling the vibration in the souls of Romanians at home and everywhere, we could not celebrate these holy days without remembering more fully the past and those who came before us. First of all Saint Andrew, the First-Called to the apostleship, who left us as an inheritance the true teaching of the Son of God in the cities of the Pontus Euxinus, in Scythia Minor, today’s Dobrogea. Saint Andrew ordained bishops and priests, and these consecrated servants, true followers of the Apostle, besides preaching the Gospel from the holy ambons of the Orthodox Church for centuries on end, urged the people of God toward unity.

In the fullness of time, this holy unity was achieved largely thanks to their contribution, that of the shepherds, who, being obedient, came down from the mountains and the valleys of Moldavia, Transylvania and Wallachia and gathered in great numbers on December 1, 1918 to bring about the UNION!

In Seattle, for the Centennial, during the Divine Liturgy on December 2, 2018 we prayed for the whole Romanian nation and for all our forebears who did something for the country, and we also raised prayers of thanksgiving to the Good God for all things. He so beautifully arranged that on this day our brothers from the other Romanian church in the city, belonging to another Orthodox jurisdiction, honored us at our celebration, creating an atmosphere of prayer and special spiritual experience that lifted our souls up to Heaven! See, then, brothers, how much union can do, UNION! We prayed to Saint Andrew to keep us united around Christ in the Orthodox Church and to pass on to us some of his missionary zeal; then, to the sound of the toaca, as is our custom on feast days, we went down to the social hall where, around lunchtime, we watched a film related to the event.

The artists of the “Datina” group brought emotion and joy to our souls, delighting us with moments of folk dance, song and poetry. Thinking of our forebears, yet looking to the future at the children present, we hope that this time, too, we passed on to them a good lesson, so that they also understand that, being Romanians, we come from a chosen and holy nation, from a noble stock, with roots deeply planted in history, with profound faith in God and with longing for the heavenly dwellings, having as examples to follow not some newer figures, rather too bold with holy things, such as a Stork, Munzer, Luther or Smith, but an Andrew the First-Called, who also Christianized us, a Constantin Brâncoveanu, the Wallachian ruler and great martyr, a Michael, the martyr of Turda, or His Highness Stephen of Moldavia, the great ruler, founder of holy places and lover of his people and country, or so many, many forebears who followed the path of Christ in a life of ascetic struggle and holiness. Such as Daniel the Hermit of Putna and Voroneț, the wonderful counselor, John the Wallachian, the pure young man, an example of Christian morality, and continuing with all the martyrs of the nation and the brave heroes in whose veins flowed Christian and Romanian blood… down to those grandparents who set out on foot for Alba Iulia, and others after them, locked up in jails and prisons, while not forgetting the Romanians who have been present in these places for more than 100 years.

Surely, another hundred years from now, some of the little ones present at the events of these days will have stories to tell to the descendants of their descendants and of ours, proud that through them, too, the spirit of UNITY, of faith and of nation is passed on, along with the stock through which Romanian Christian blood flows, in these places too or wherever they may be…

 

Protosyngellos Andrei Aioanei

title: Centennial Events at Saints Peter and Paul Church, Astoria, New York
intro:
The year 2018 carried a special emotional charge and a historical and spiritual significance for all Romanians, whether private individuals or institutions.

In preparation for the centennial of the Great Union of 1918 and the great celebrations dedicated to this historic year, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas encouraged all the priests under his obedience to organize events in their parishes connected with this important historical act.

In this context, at Saints Peter and Paul Church in New York, Fr. Prof. Theodor Damian organized a centennial event every month (symposia, round tables, presentations, etc.), inviting intellectuals from the Romanian community of New York, as well as from Romania, to lecture on topics related to the events that took place in each month of the  year 1918.

These events were held under the auspices of the Academy of Romanian Scientists, USA Branch, the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, and the Romanian Institute of Orthodox Theology and Spirituality of New York.

Details about these events are available here.

title: First Divine Liturgy in the New Church of the Resurrection of the Lord Parish in Sacramento, CA
intro:
In explaining the parable of the sower (Luke 8,5-15), our Savior Jesus Christ describes the kinds of souls upon which the seed of His life-giving word is sown. As a young priest, for years, whenever I read this parable at the Divine Liturgy, my attention was focused mainly on the attitude toward the seed generously sown by the sower, the drama of the “places” not prepared enough to bear fruit. In the search every priest undertakes while preparing his Sunday sermon, to bring new meanings or to look for deeper things not noticed before, at some point my attention was drawn to what is said about the seed that fell on “good ground”. The Savior says of it that it bears fruit “with patience”. So something more is needed besides the seed and the good ground, something very important in the economy of bearing fruit: patience.

In a way, I think it is forgivable that we do not focus our attention on the virtue of patience in our youth. The zeal and energy of youth have a hard time understanding this virtue, seemingly motionless and fixed, which does not lead immediately to results. Time and age, however, usually put us where we belong. The New Testament teaches that perfect patience belongs to the Father Himself, of whom we say that He is “longsuffering”. The Son is sent in “the fullness of the time” and not just at any time, and toward sinners He shows longsuffering. So this virtue of patience must not be belittled, but valued as a qualification our soul and mind acquire over time.

On Sunday, December 16, 2018, we, the priest and faithful of the Resurrection of the Lord Parish in Sacramento, rejoiced in the fruits gained through patience: obtaining approval to use our new church. Our joy was increased by the fact that we entered our new church accompanied by our hierarch, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae. The blessing was complete and the joy pure and holy. We did not enter what is from now on “our” church alone, but accompanied by the blessing of obedience and by the gifts with which God has comforted our hearts. Our exodus is over. From now on, the Gospel and the Antimension can rest on a new Holy Table, and the travel bag in which we kept the Holy Vessels is no longer needed.

Looking back, it should be mentioned that the journey of our church began in 2002, when a handful of Romanians, led by Mr. John Roșca, wished for a Romanian church belonging to the Romanian Patriarchate. After several unsuccessful attempts to have a church of our own, our church community was hosted, beginning in the summer of 2009, by the Christians of “Saint George Melkite Greek-Catholic Church” in Sacramento. Because we began the Divine Liturgy at 1:00 pm, some of the faithful could no longer attend. Those who stayed close were the very devoted, with the unshakable hope that God would not abandon us and that at some point in the future we would have our own church.

The year 2011, a year of economic recession, was for us a year of abundance and blessing. Even though, personally, a good number of our church’s faithful went through the hardship of losing their homes or jobs, property values being very low, through a determined effort we managed to pool our resources or lend to one another, interest-free, enough money to buy the current property at 3250 U St., Antelope, in cash. Over the following two years we managed to pay back all the borrowed money and to begin the long and costly process of converting the property’s status from residential to commercial. This process, from the purchase of the building to the last final inspection, lasted, as Mr. Horia Groza notes, 7 years, 7 months and 22 days.

Throughout this time, our waiting and patience were strengthened and sustained by the visits His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae made to our community, and by the prayers, blessings and good spirit he instilled in all of us. Today’s results prove that what I said above is not just a polite formula of protocol, but that the prayers and blessings we received were power and grace at work. Even though in the last two months the outcome was somewhat foreseeable, the moment of final approval and the end of the convoluted inspection process came, as we all felt, like “a gift from above,” like a release from bondage.

We thank God for comforting our hearts with this joy. We thank His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae for his help in prayer and his blessing. We thank one another in this bond of brotherhood and unity, and from now on we seek to dare to look higher, as our hierarch counseled us in his homily, namely that the full joy of the Christian life is attaining the Kingdom of Heaven. We experienced a beautiful coincidence between the Sunday Gospel reading, the parable of those invited to the supper, and the call to all the Orthodox Romanians of Sacramento to our new church.

Fr. Teodor Gârlonța, Parish Priest

title: Spiritual Retreat in San Antonio, Texas
intro:
With the blessing of His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae, a few days of spiritual retreat took place at Saint John Cassian Mission in San Antonio from December 14 to 16, 2018. This spiritual event enjoyed pan-Orthodox participation by priests and faithful from the San Antonio area, with Rev. Fr. Alessandro Margheritino as guide and preacher.

Fr. Alessandro was born and raised in Palermo, Italy, in a Catholic family, and converted to Orthodoxy at the age of 18 through His Grace Bishop Siluan of the Romanian Orthodox Diocese of Italy. After earning his degree in International Relations - Political Science at the University of Palermo, he moved to the USA and married Miss Ana Edelman, the daughter of Russian emigrants from Moscow. From the moment he embraced Orthodoxy he wished to study theology, and so, at the urging of His Grace Siluan, he enrolled at Saint Vladimir’s Orthodox Theological Seminary in New York, from which he graduated with outstanding results. After completing his studies he was ordained a priest, and today he is the parish priest of Saint Innocent Church in Olmsted Falls, Ohio, of the OCA, and President of the Orthodox Clergy Council of Cleveland. Fr. Alessandro carries out a rich publishing and pastoral-missionary activity and is invited to numerous conferences on Orthodox theology and spirituality.

Drawing on his experience of converting from Catholicism to Orthodoxy in Italy, as well as on his time over the years in Romanian, Russian, Greek and American Orthodox communities, Fr. Alessandro gave, over three days, several spiritual meditations on the theme “Unity in Christ and Pan-Orthodox Work”.

The program began on Friday evening with the service of Holy Unction and ended with the second catechesis for the Nativity Fast recommended by the Diocesan Center, on The spirituality of the family: prayer, fasting, liturgical participation.

Saturday morning began with the Divine Liturgy, followed by the first meditation, entitled “That they may be one”. Starting from the Savior’s High Priestly Prayer in the Gospel of John 17:21-23, Fr. Alessandro presented the model of the Unity of the Holy Trinity and explained that Christ’s Sacrifice on the Cross was offered, and will be offered until the Second Coming, for the unity of the Church. When we humans get angry with one another and let our pride rule us, we are in fact turning our backs on the Sacrifice of the Cross.

After lunch, prepared by the ladies’ committee for all participants, we took part in the second session, entitled “What can I do for the unity of the Body of Christ”. In this second meditation session, Fr. Alessandro spoke about the call to unity in the Epistles of the Holy Apostle Paul and referred especially to the Epistle to the Philippians 2:2-4, which urges us to have the same love, being of one accord, of one mind, doing nothing through selfish ambition or conceit, but in lowliness of mind and caring for one another. Finally, Fr. Alessandro shared with us the pastoral-missionary experience of the Orthodox priests in the Cleveland, Ohio area and brought to our attention a number of useful pieces of information for better pan-Orthodox cooperation and for intensifying the mission to the heterodox. 

On Sunday the Baptismal Divine Liturgy was celebrated, and together with the catechumen Paul we shared a special moment, both through the particular rite and through the catechesis on Holy Baptism as the moment of our spiritual birth and of becoming part of the one body, the Church of Christ.  

We give glory to God for all things and thank His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae for his support and encouragement.

Fr. Valentin Ilieș, Parish Priest

title: Carols at SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago, December 2018
intro:
The first carolers have arrived at SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago. His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was caroled by the children of the Cathedral’s Romanian Saturday School and Sunday School on Saturday, December 22, 2018. Led by their teachers, the children sang of the star in the east, of the Magi and of the shepherds. His Eminence Nicolae thanked the children and the teachers and gave them small icons, sweets and fruit.

On Sunday, December 23, the children and youth of SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago will present the Christmas program. More than 100 children of the Romanian School and the Sunday School are ready to take the stage in the Cathedral’s social hall. Divided into 6 groups, ranging in age from 2 to 18, the children and youth of the Cathedral will bring to the parents and faithful of the Cathedral the Good News of the Nativity of the Savior, in the hope that Santa Claus will come this year as well with beautiful gifts.

The Choir of SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago is ready, as every year, for the carol concert on Christmas Eve, Monday, December 24. The repertoire includes traditional Romanian carols as well as several carols from the international repertoire. The young members of the Cathedral choir have rehearsed diligently to offer the Romanian Orthodox faithful of the Chicago metropolitan area the joy of receiving the news of the Nativity of the Lord through carols. Christmas Eve is a special evening of the church year. That is why the carol concert of the Choir of SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago, on Christmas Eve itself, is a much-awaited event. After the concert in the church, the carolers will continue to proclaim the Nativity of the Lord at the homes of all those who wish to receive them. The first to be caroled will be His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, who will receive the carolers, together with the clergy of the Cathedral, at the diocesan residence.

title: The Nativity of the Lord Celebrated at SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago, December 2018
intro:
This year, too, the feast of the Nativity of the Lord was celebrated in Chicago with great joy and many events. On Sunday, December 23, 2018, the more than 100 children of the Sunday School and the Romanian Language School caroled the faithful of SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago. The carol Moș Crăciun was sung again and again while waiting for Santa Claus to arrive with gifts for all the children.

Christmas Eve was blessed by the celebration of the Christmas Vespers, followed by the carol concert of the Cathedral choir. The repertoire included traditional Romanian carols and several carols from the international repertoire. The joy of proclaiming the Nativity of the Lord through carols was shared with all those present, a pleasant surprise thanks to the quality and richness of the repertoire and the participation of the children in the concert program. Christmas Eve continued with caroling at people’s homes, the first stop being His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae at the episcopal residence.

Christmas Day, Tuesday, December 25, was an occasion of great spiritual joy. SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago was filled with faithful eager to take part in the feast in its liturgical setting. During the homily, His Eminence Nicolae spoke about the joy of proclaiming the Nativity of the Lord through carols and hymns, about discovering the meanings of the mystery of the Incarnation with the help of Saint Gregory Palamas, and about bearing witness to the news of the Nativity of the Lord to our fellow human beings.

The feast of the Nativity of the Lord continued in Chicago on Wednesday and Thursday with the celebration of the Divine Liturgy on the second and third days of Christmas, respectively. On Wednesday evening, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, together with the priests and a group of faithful of the Cathedral, went to carol our Romanian brothers and sisters living in nursing homes in the Chicago area. The caroling brought great joy to those who wait with much hope for any visit and word of greeting. On the feast of the Holy First Martyr and Archdeacon Stephen, Dean Fr. Călin Barbolovici of Holy Trinity Parish in Troy, Michigan, served at SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago, alongside His Eminence Nicolae and the priests of the Cathedral.

title: Christmas Traditions and Customs at Holy Emperors Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago, December 30, 2018
intro:
For the sixth year in a row, on December 30, 2018, Holy Emperors Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago hosted its program of Christmas traditions and customs. Just as in times past, when the children of the village set out with the star from the priest’s house, where they received his blessing, and then went caroling to every household in the village, so too did lovers of Romanian traditions gather at the Cathedral in Chicago and begin the greetings and carols. The hosts of the event, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae and the priests and faithful of the Cathedral, were dressed for the feast in a setting depicting the story of the Nativity of the Lord in the manger in Bethlehem. And because the beauty of the Christmas feasts lies in going caroling and proclaiming the Birth of Christ, we also welcomed carolers from Romania, the group Glasuri Ardelene and Cornel Borza with his ensemble from Bihor.

The traditions, customs and carols that gladdened our hearts came from Transylvania, Bessarabia, Moldavia and Muntenia, and the national costumes came from all over the country. The youngest carolers, the children of the Cathedral, were also present in national costume and greeted us with the sorcova, wishing us all the best in the New Year. The warm atmosphere conveyed that our national identity is well defined and that, even far from home, we have not forgotten that we are Romanian. In fact, just as we have ended this event for 6 years now, everyone present sang: “Nu uita că eşti român/Că sus în deal la tine-n sat, Popa Ioan te-a botezat.”

For the two hours the event lasted, our thoughts traveled to the Romanian village of old, “there” becoming “here”: “Here every thought is slower and your heart beats more rarely, as if it beat not in your chest but somewhere deep in the earth,” as Blaga writes, in the village where eternity was born.

title: Missionary Visit of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae to South Carolina and Georgia
intro:
One year ago, through the efforts of a dedicated group of Romanian Orthodox Christians and with the support of Fr. Nicolae Clempuș, the Romanian Orthodox Mission of Saint Gregory the Theologian, whose feast is celebrated on January 25, was established in the city of Greenville, South Carolina. This year, on the occasion of the first patronal feast of the Mission, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was in the midst of the faithful of Greenville.

The missionary visit took place on Saturday, January 26, 2019, and began with the Holy Akathist of Saint Gregory the Theologian, the patron of the mission, continuing with the Hierarchical Divine Liturgy. The parishioners of the young Mission took part with great emotion in their first Hierarchical Divine Liturgy and received their Hierarch with great warmth of heart. Young families with children, older and younger, gathered at St. Mary Coptic Church, the temporary host of this Mission, to partake of the grace and blessing of God.

In his homily, Metropolitan Nicolae gave edifying advice for the proper organization and functioning of the future Romanian parish in Greenville. He emphasized the spiritual Church, which is made up of the unity and harmony of its parishioners, and the building up of the invisible Church based on the Mysteries of God. In conclusion, His Eminence Nicolae officially handed over to the serving priest the new and first holy Antimension of the Mission, on which the Divine Liturgy will be celebrated from now on.

After the Divine Liturgy and a memorial service, all the faithful were invited to a fellowship meal prepared and served in exemplary fashion by the ladies of the Mission.

Pastoral Visit to the Protection of the Mother of God Parish in the Atlanta Area

In the northern part of the Atlanta metropolitan area there is a Romanian Church which for 18 years has been making its way toward salvation and gathers all the Orthodox Christians of the area in a beautiful church built under the holy omophorion of the Mother of God. St. Mary’s Church in Dacula, whose patronal feast is the Protection of the Mother of God, receives with great emotion, at the beginning of each year, the visit of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae. This year, Metropolitan Nicolae, together with a group of priests, celebrated the Mystery of Holy Unction on the evening of Saturday, January 26, 2019. In a world facing illness, not only bodily but above all spiritual, the mystery of healing through anointing with holy oil gathered more than 200 faithful in St. Mary’s Church, who, alongside the Hierarch and the priests, knelt in prayer. After the service, His Eminence Nicolae delivered a homily emphasizing the importance of our spiritual health and our struggle against sin, which is the true illness. The faithful were anointed 7 times with holy oil and received hierarchical blessings.

On Sunday, January 27, the faithful of the parish were called to the Hierarchical Divine Liturgy, at which Fr. Nicolae Clempuș, the parish priest, and Fr. Theodor Regoș served alongside His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae. There is a spiritual thirst among the Romanian Orthodox Christians of the southeastern United States, a desire to receive properly, and to have in the midst of the community, the Primate of the Romanian Orthodox Church in America. The church was full, and the Divine Liturgy comforted the souls of those present. The entire community of faithful at St. Mary’s was involved in the preparations for the pastoral visit. From decorating the church with flowers, to serving coffee and refreshments after the service, to the official meal organized on the occasion of our Hierarch’s visit, everyone took part and gave of their time to the Church and, through it, directly to Christ.

In his homily, His Eminence Nicolae spoke about perseverance in prayer, in view of all the obstacles of the world in which we live, about the healing of the blind man of Jericho, and about how the healed blind man becomes a symbol of all mankind before Christ, deprived of the light of the knowledge of God. The hierarchical visit ended with a festive meal and a meeting with the members of the Parish Council, who, together with the parish priest, oversee the projects of the parish.

Fr. Nicolae Clempuș

title: Patronal Feast of St. Simeon Romanian Orthodox Church in Westland, MI
intro:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell  together in unity! (Psalm 132, 1).
…for where there is unity, there the Lord commanded the blessing and life forevermore.” (Psalm 132, 3)

 Brethren dwelling together was fulfilled at the patronal feast of “Saint Simeon” Romanian Orthodox Church in Westland, MI, in the Detroit area, on February 2, the great Feast of the Meeting of the Lord, and on Sunday, February 3, when we celebrated the patronal feast of our “Saint Simeon” Church, with our father, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, present at all the services in response to our church’s invitation. And so we were able to see that “where there is unity, there the Lord commanded the blessing and life forevermore” (Psalm 132, 3).

His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae served the Akathist of the Meeting of the Lord on Saturday evening at 5:00 PM, together with a synod of priests: Dean Fr. Călin Barbolovici of “Holy Trinity” Church in Troy, MI, Fr. Ștefan Vlad of “Saint Parascheva of Sihla” Church in Royal Oak, MI, and Fr. Aurel Sas of “Saint Simeon” Church. After the Akathist, His Eminence Nicolae delivered the homily. Fr. Aurel Sas offered words of welcome to the hierarch. His Eminence then held a conversation with the members of the Parish Council and the faithful of the church who were present.

On Sunday, February 3, His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae was welcomed by Fr. Aurel Sas with the Holy Gospel and the Holy Cross, by a group of children who offered him flowers, and by the faithful with “bread and salt”, according to our Romanian tradition. The hierarch then served the Divine Liturgy together with Dean Fr. Călin and Fr. Aurel, and at the end of the hierarchical Liturgy His Eminence delivered a homily to the faithful, drawing together the Gospel readings of the previous Sundays with that of Zacchaeus the tax collector, which truly edified the multitude of the faithful spiritually.

This was followed by the patronal feast service of “Saint Simeon” Church, according to the tradition of the Banat, in which two families, wearing the Romanian Tricolor, served as sponsors of the feast. After the service, “Many Years!” was sung for His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae and for the leaders and faithful of the church.

Fr. Aurel Sas gave thanks to the good God for the blessings poured out upon our church, and to His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan Nicolae for his canonical visit and for his care for “Saint Simeon” Church as it advances on the path of salvation in Christ the Savior.

Fr. Aurel briefly presented what the faithful of the church had accomplished over the course of a year with the Lord’s help, among them the iconostasis, which is soon to be adorned with icons. His Eminence Nicolae was invited to consecrate the iconostasis at the proper time.

His Eminence then blessed the festive meal, donated by the families of Simi and Mariana Jude and of Mihai and Diana Băloi, who were this year’s sponsors of the patronal feast. After the prayer of thanksgiving, His Eminence returned to the Metropolia residence in Chicago.

We pray to the merciful God to bless us in the future as well, through the prayers of Saint Simeon, who was found worthy to receive the Infant Jesus in his arms in the Temple in Jerusalem, forty days after His birth.

 

Fr. Aurel Sas

title: His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae Served at Lainici Monastery, Gorj County, Romania
intro:
With the blessing of His Eminence Metropolitan Irineu of Oltenia, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was in the midst of the monastic community of Lainici Monastery, Gorj County, on Sunday, February 24, 2019, the 34th Sunday after Pentecost (of the Prodigal Son). His Eminence Nicolae attended the Vigil service on Saturday evening and celebrated the Divine Liturgy on Sunday together with the Abbot, Archimandrite Ioachim, and the clergy of the monastery.

In his sermon, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae interpreted the parable of the Prodigal Son, speaking first about the 10-week period of preparation for Holy Pascha and the steps of the spiritual ascent we are called to climb toward the Resurrection. He then noted that the parable is found in chapter 15 of the Holy Gospel according to Luke and, together with the parables of the lost sheep and the lost coin, expresses the indescribable joy of the Heavenly Father at the return of sinners. Interpreting the stages of the prodigal son’s repentance, His Eminence Nicolae urged the faithful, parents and grandparents, to build, together with the servants of the Church, a spiritual home for their children and grandchildren, to which they will want to return if they go astray in this world that has drifted far from God.

The Abbot, Fr. Ioachim, thanked His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae for serving and, with the blessing of His Eminence Metropolitan Irineu, presented him with fragments of the relics of Saint Irodion of Lainici together with an icon of the saint. Fr. Ioachim recounted the life of Saint Irodion, disciple and later spiritual father of Saint Callinicus of Cernica, as well as the story of the finding of Saint Irodion’s relics on May 10, 2009.

His Eminence Nicolae thanked His Eminence Irineu for the blessing to serve and for the holy relics, and the Abbot and the monastic community for their welcome and for serving together. He then expressed gratitude, on behalf of the Romanian Orthodox priests and faithful in America, for the precious gift of the holy relics.

title: Sunday of Orthodoxy in Cleveland, Ohio
intro:
This year the first Sunday of Great Lent, the Sunday of Orthodoxy, a day of great Christian significance, was a double celebration for us in Cleveland. His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was present at Annunciation Parish to ordain to the priesthood Deacon Petru Neaga, who has served at our Cathedral for more than a year. Since it was the Sunday of Orthodoxy, toward the end of the Divine Liturgy, after the Prayer behind the Ambo, the children and young people of the Sunday School made a procession in the church carrying holy icons. It was a moving procession, both for the children and young people and for the faithful present.

The second moment of the day followed. On the evening of the Sunday of Orthodoxy, in keeping with a tradition of many years in Cleveland, Vespers was held, organized by the Greater Cleveland Council of Orthodox Clergy (GCCOC). The host was Saint Michael Orthodox Parish (OCA), shepherded by Fr. John Memorich. As he was in Cleveland, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was invited to preside over the service. Present were 19 priests, 1 deacon (Deacon Aurel Pâra of the Diocesan Center in Chicago) and a large number of faithful. The sermon of the day was given by Archimandrite Joseph Morris, Abbot of Saint Gregory Palamas Greek Orthodox Monastery in Perrysville, Ohio.

At the end of Vespers, in a short message, His Eminence Nicolae urged the faithful to become confessors of the Orthodox Christian faith in today’s world. The evening ended with a Lenten agape meal offered by the host parish.

Fr. Ion Gherman

title: Spiritual Retreat at Protection of the Mother of God Monastery, Allegan, MI
intro:
From March 29 to 31, 2019, a wonderful spiritual retreat was held, with the blessing of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae, at the Protection of the Mother of God women’s monastery in Allegan, Michigan. About 30 ladies took part, faithful from the parishes of the Romanian Orthodox Archdiocese of the United States of America in the Deanery of the Central USA. The retreat was an initiative of AROLA, the Ladies’ Association of the Metropolia.

The theme of this gathering was “The Responsibility of the Christian Woman between Tradition and Modernity,” and the speaker was Hieromonk Atanasie Popescu, the monastery’s spiritual father, who presented an extensive, carefully prepared talk. Building on it, young mothers and others raised general and personal issues and exchanged views and impressions. The participants addressed this highly topical, vast, intricate and winding subject with great seriousness and interest.

One would have wished the warm, relaxed and friendly atmosphere to go on for many more hours. However, the retreat program also included other activities: services (Vespers, Akathists, a memorial service, Matins, the Divine Liturgy, Confession), as well as recreation in the midst of nature. After the three days spent at our new monastery of the Protection of the Mother of God, we returned to our homes cleaner, richer and more rested in soul. And, of course, with the wish to return as soon as possible.

Elena Picioiu

title: The Feast of the Lord’s Resurrection in New York
intro:
The Resurrection of the Lord, also called the feast of Pascha, is the oldest feast of Christendom. It is the feast that brought humanity the hope of salvation and of eternal life, through the sacrifice of Christ the Savior. The Resurrection of the Lord gives meaning to life and courage for the passage from this life to eternal life.

The Romanian faithful of the Parish of Saint Nicholas the Hierarch and Saint George in New York greeted the feast of the Lord’s Resurrection with great joy. As every year, hundreds of Romanian faithful, joined by small groups of Greeks and Russians, came at midnight to receive the Holy Light. Faith in the Resurrection of the Lord united all those present in one mind and one voice.

At midnight, the parish priest offered the Holy Light to all the faithful present. On a stage set up in front of the church, the Resurrection service began with the reading of the Holy Gospel, after which the Paschal Pastoral Letter of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was read. The Paschal greeting Christ is risen! and Truly He is risen! rang out powerfully from everyone’s hearts.

At the end, Fr. Marius Dumitrescu urged the people to repentance and good deeds, reminding them that the fast from food had ended, but the spiritual fast must continue. “With our life, with what we have gathered in our soul, let us seek to be good people who can inspire trust in others, and true confessors of Orthodoxy. May God help us!” He then thanked all those present and urged them to stay until the end of the service so that he could bless them.

The liturgical program then continued in the church with Matins and the Divine Liturgy, attended by many of those who had come before midnight. To the glory of God and to our joy, a large number of faithful and children received Holy Communion at the Divine Liturgy. Many of them came dressed in Romanian folk costumes. The service ended with the Paschal fellowship meal, where everyone could enjoy our traditional Romanian dishes.

Fr. Marius Dumitrescu

title: Feast of Holy Pascha in Chicago
intro:
As every year, the feast of Holy Pascha was an occasion of great joy for the community of the Metropolitan Cathedral of SS. Constantine and Helen in Chicago. After the services appointed for Holy Week, a multitude of Romanian Orthodox faithful took part in the service of the Resurrection of the Lord. At midnight, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae gave the light to the clergy and faithful. This was followed by the procession around the church, the reading of the Holy Gospel and the litany in front of the church. His Eminence Nicolae wished those present light, joy and peace: “May the light of the Resurrection illumine your life, may the joy of the proclamation of life’s victory over death gladden your souls and bring peace to your families and to the whole world. Go and proclaim to all the light, joy and peace of the Resurrection of the Lord.”

The Paschal Canon continued in the church, followed by the Divine Liturgy. The responses were sung by the youth group and the Cathedral choir. Many faithful received Holy Communion, fulfilling the effort of the seven-week fast. At the end of the Divine Liturgy, His Eminence Nicolae spoke about the joy of the feast brought by Christ through the victory of life over death, quoting Saint Nikolai Velimirovich: “‘Now all things are filled with light: heaven and earth and the places beneath the earth.’ Christ, the Son of God, takes upon Himself our human nature enslaved by sin in order to turn it back toward God, to restore its dignity and to free it from sin and death. Through the Incarnation and the Resurrection, human nature is healed, renewed and given back the chance of eternity… Through the Resurrection, Christ has become the greatest Physician in the history of humankind, for He has brought us healing from an illness more terrible than all illnesses, which is sin. The medicine against sin is He Himself, the Risen Lord.”

According to the rubrics, on Sunday afternoon the Agape Vespers of the Resurrection, also called the second Resurrection, was served. After the Gospel was read in several languages, His Eminence Nicolae explained the meaning of the proclamation of peace and of the power of the forgiveness of sins to all nations. The traditional Paschal fraternal agape meal concluded Resurrection Sunday at SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago.

On the second and third days of Pascha, the clergy of the SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago were joined by Protosyngellos Andrei Aioanei, who formerly served at the Cathedral, and by Rev. Fr. Petru Neaga, the new parish priest of Annunciation Parish in Olmsted Township, Ohio. His Eminence Nicolae further unfolded the meanings of the feast of Holy Pascha by referring to the call to joy and courage addressed by the Risen Christ to the Myrrh-bearing Women, and to the knowledge through participation of God revealed to the disciples traveling to Emmaus when He made Himself known in the Holy Eucharist. On this occasion, Fr. Petru was elevated to the rank of confessor so that he may fully take on his new mission.

title: Pope Francis Met with Patriarch Daniel and the Members of the Permanent Synod
full:
On Friday, May 30, 2019, Pope Francis met with His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel and the members of the Permanent Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church.

The meeting took place at the Patriarchal Palace, in the context of the three-day visit that the Head of the Roman Catholic Church is making to Romania. The meeting was also attended by His Eminence Nicolae, Romanian Orthodox Metropolitan of the Americas, and His Grace Ioan Casian, Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Canada.

The delegation led by Pope Francis arrived at Patriarchal Hill at around 3:45 PM and was welcomed by Patriarch Daniel in the Europa Christiana Hall of the Patriarchal Palace, in the presence of the hierarchs of the Permanent Synod.

After the introduction of the two delegations, a private meeting took place between His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel and Pope Francis.

Then, in the Conventus Hall, the official addresses for this event were delivered.

The Patriarch of Romania referred to the meeting between Patriarch Teoctist and Pope John Paul II.

“Our predecessors call us today as well to defend and promote faith in Christ and Christian values in a highly secularized Europe, in order to pass on to the young generation faith in the merciful love of Christ for the world and faith in the eternal life of the human person.”

In his address, Pope Francis reiterated the importance of Pope John Paul II’s visit to Romania, which he called “an Easter gift, an event that contributed not only to the revival of relations between Orthodox and Catholics in Romania, but also to the dialogue between Catholics and Orthodox in general.”

He also emphasized that “the bonds of faith that unite us go back to the Apostles, the witnesses of the Risen One, in particular to the bond that united Peter and Andrew, who, according to tradition, brought the faith to these lands.”

The meeting at the Patriarchate ended at around 4:45 PM and was followed by Pope Francis’s visit to the National Cathedral.

title: Religion Olympiad Results, 2019
intro:
With the blessing of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas and of His Grace Bishop Ioan Casian, Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Canada,  on Sunday, May 12, 2019, the final stage of the tenth Religion Olympiad, 2019 edition, took place in six metropolitan centers in the USA and Canada and two special centers. The written parish round on April 7, 2019 was taken by 132 children, and 89 candidates took part in the parishes that hosted the metropolitan-center round: 49 in the 8-12 age group and 40 young people in the 13-18 age group. The general theme was: “Salvation: the union of man with God through faith, the fulfilling of the commandments (almsgiving) and the receiving of the divine grace of the Holy Mysteries.”

The tests were based on the new 2018-2019 curriculum of the parish schools. Thanks are due to the Education Committee of our Holy Metropolia, which organized and prepared the tests, especially Mr. Stelian Ghinea of Rochester NY and Mrs. Ileana Gavriș and Mrs. Veronica Ciocan of Edmonton AB, to the teachers in the two grading centers, and to all the teachers on the parish and metropolitan-center committees involved in this edition. A word of appreciation is also due to the eight parishes that joyfully hosted the tenth edition of the Religion Olympiad.

Each candidate will receive a diploma from our hierarchs, and the first-place winners in each category received a free voucher to attend the Metropolia’s summer camp in Allegan MI.

title: Saint John Jacob: Protector of the Nuns in America
intro:
This year (2019), the community of the Protection of the Mother of God Monastery for nuns in Allegan, Michigan, honored its second patron, the newly shining saint of the Romanian Orthodox Church and intercessor for the whole world: John Jacob of Neamț. This is the first patronal feast celebrated since monastic life began at this holy monastery in January.

As early as Friday, the faithful began arriving at the monastery, where they could enjoy the beautiful countryside reminiscent of Romania, especially for those who long for the places of home. On Saturday evening Great Vespers with Litiya was celebrated, and on Sunday Matins and the Divine Liturgy, with chanters from Chicago and Detroit also taking part. The pilgrims had the opportunity to cleanse their souls through the Sacrament of Confession and also had the joy of receiving the Body and Blood of the Lord Jesus Christ, as is fitting, especially during this period of the Dormition Fast.

Throughout the weekend, the pilgrims listened several times to poems and teachings of Saint John Jacob, at times interpreted by the monastery’s spiritual father, Hieromonk Atanasie. The pilgrims were glad to learn the beautiful thoughts that sprang from the God-loving heart of Saint John, who, although he lived in seclusion in monasteries, sketes and caves in the Holy Land, knew very well the social and political realities of his time and the temptations facing the faithful in the world.

The saint advised those in the diaspora not to taste the “pretzels of the red regime. These pretzels are dyed with the martyrs’ blood of our believing brothers in the homeland. They now suffer like slaves at forced labor, and from their sweat and blood bribes are kneaded for propaganda.” The saint also warned of the danger of the evolutionist ideologies wreaking havoc in the world: “Today the sacks of science / are filled with inventions. But of the mysteries of faith / the world no longer has any news! / All the striving of the world / is to prove / That: ‘Matter is everything, / The Spirit has nowhere to be’!”; as well as of the comfort that kills the ascetic spirit, of technological progress at the expense of spiritual progress, and of dependence on new technologies, warnings that seem even more timely today than in the 1950s when they were written: “The world of the new fashion / puts cotton in its ears / when it hears in the churches / only the old songs! / Don’t you have a radio? it says / to the hermit’s cap, / how do you live like this in vain / without a trace of progress? / The world today moves forward / with the means of living! / You’ve fallen behind, father, / thinking only of Paradise!  … On Sunday to the service / Christians hardly come, / but the movie theater / is always full.”

For this year’s pilgrims, the monastery community prepared many icons of various saints of our Church, prayer ropes and woven crosses, and as a gift everyone received three bookmarks printed with the image of the Venerable John and with poems written by the saint, to encourage knowledge of the beautiful life and thought of this great Saint of the Romanians and of Orthodox Christians everywhere.

“Wandering sons of my country,
Troubled among strangers,
Do not forget your calling
As Romanians and as Christians.”

title: The Romanian Village, Keeper of Our Spiritual Values, Calls Us to Help It!
intro:
12.08. 2019

The Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church has declared 2019 the Homage Year of the Romanian Village (of Priests, Teachers and Good Steward Mayors) and the Commemorative Year of Patriarchs Nicodim Munteanu and Iustin Moisescu and of the Translators of Church Books. This initiative sought to highlight that the village is also the place where many of the spiritual, cultural and identity values handed down to our day were formed and preserved over time.

In this sense, honoring the Romanian village and its major contribution to the historical development of the Romanian people is both a necessity and a great dignity. Romanian villages, with their churches and peasant houses, their cemeteries and graves guarded by crosses, their lanes and welcoming gates, carry a mysterious and visible language of tradition, of the physical and spiritual continuity of this nation; they are mirrors of the Romanian soul, revealing today, as the case may be, our diligence or our neglect, our responsibility or our indifference.

When we speak of the need to sanctify the time of our earthly life in order to attain salvation, we see how, in the village, more than in the city, life is understood as a blessed time for sanctifying the place where we live. And if we sanctify the place where we live on earth, we can hope to receive a place in heaven as well, “a little corner of paradise,” as Father Paisie Olaru of Sihăstria Monastery in Neamț used to say.

Unfortunately, it is clear to all of us that the Romanian village today is no longer what it was many years ago. At the same time, it cannot be said that nothing of what existed in the past can be recovered or cultivated today. The deepest crisis the Romanian peasant is experiencing at present is the suffering of being uprooted and estranged through emigration abroad, working more for the development of other countries than for his own homeland. The places of their birth are being abandoned by the young generations, and solidarity among people is ever weaker, as villagers become estranged from their own land and from their own identity.

For this reason, the Romanian Orthodox Church supports the Romanian village, organizing mutual aid programs and mobilizing the faithful to help the poor, the elderly and the sick. Where there is close cooperation between the priest, the mayor, the teacher and the doctor, greater hope and deeper spiritual communion are born.

In this context, the HEALTH FOR VILLAGES Project is also being carried out in support of rural areas, organized by the Romanian Patriarchate in partnership with the Ministry of Health, a project initiated and developed mainly by volunteers from the Chapel of the People’s Salvation Cathedral and extended throughout the entire Romanian Patriarchate. This project, which has so far benefited more than eight thousand village residents, most of them elderly and sick, brings together the enthusiasm and availability of volunteers with the good cooperation of village parish priests and mayors, thus mobilizing the rural population to benefit from free medical consultations.

Consequently, there is a clear need for stronger solidarity between urban and rural parishes, and between the parishes and communities of Romanian Orthodox faithful abroad and the parishes of Romanian villages, as well as for greater cooperation with local, regional and central authorities, in order to support and improve village life.

On the occasion of the Sunday of Romanian Migrants, we congratulate all the hierarchs and servants of the Romanian Orthodox Holy Altars abroad for their pastoral and missionary work of preserving and cultivating the Orthodox Christian faith and Romanian spiritual, cultural and identity values. We also pray to the merciful God to grant all Romanians living among foreigners health and joy, peace and much help in the good deed of supporting their loved ones in Romania.

With appreciation and fatherly blessing,

† DANIEL
Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church

title: Archdeacon Adrian Sorin Mihalache to Lecture in the U.S.A., September 7-22, 2019
intro:
With the blessing of His Eminence Archbishop and Metropolitan NICOLAE and at the invitation of the Romanian Orthodox Metropolia of the Americas, Archdeacon Dr. ADRIAN SORIN MIHALACHE, Lecturer at the Faculty of Orthodox Theology in Iași, will give a series of lectures in the United States of America from September 7 to 22, 2019.

Fr. Adrian Sorin Mihalache holds degrees in mathematics and theology and has completed master’s programs in psychology, philosophy, theology and theoretical physics. Since 2010 he has held a Ph.D. in Philosophy from the “Al. I. Cuza” University of Iași, with the thesis “The Cosmic Dimension of the Person,” under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Ştefan Afloroaei. In 2013 he entered the doctoral program in medicine at the “Carol Davila” University of Medicine and Pharmacy in Bucharest, carrying out a project exploring the long-term effects of prayer from a neuroscientific perspective (2020). He is a university lecturer at the Faculty of Orthodox Theology in Iași, executive editor of the “Journal for Interdisciplinary Research on Religion and Science,” published by the Center for Advanced Interdisciplinary Research in Religion and Science of the “Al. I. Cuza” University of Iași, and coordinator of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies in Religion and Science of the “Solidaritate şi Speranţă” Foundation, and he is involved in other interdisciplinary projects and activities as well. He produces and hosts the program “Lumina celui nevăzut” on TV Trinitas of the Romanian Patriarchate, and in 2017 His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel awarded Deacon Adrian Sorin Mihalache the Order of Saint John Chrysostom for his constant contribution to the Orthodox education of young people. In July 2019 he was elevated to the rank of archdeacon by Metropolitan Teofan of Moldavia and Bukovina.

The lecture tour given by Archdeacon Adrian Sorin Mihalache aims to bring to public attention the agreement between the latest discoveries in neuroscience and the teachings of the Holy Fathers.

title: A Few Impressions from ITO Craiova 2019, the “Chalice” That Gathers Young People from All over the World
intro:
Every gathering of Orthodox youth is an occasion of Eucharistic communion, and of the ideas and feelings brought both by the dioceses within our motherland and by those of the diaspora.

Whatever their native country, people feel the need for an identity, a faith and a philosophy. Young people raised in the diaspora, or who have moved there, are like a flower cut off from its root: they need artificial nourishment to stay alive and not wither. So it is with our practicing Christian Romanian living among strangers: he finds himself in a sea of ideologies and beliefs foreign to the origins of his people. In this condition, the Orthodox believer comes into contact with foreign gods: money, the temptation of power and dishonest gain, pleasure and luxury. All of these take the place of the spiritual spring offered by the bond with our forefathers, which is found most tangibly on our Romanian soil.

Being alongside the Romanian delegates from the diaspora, I first noticed the beauty of brotherly understanding, but at the same time the sad consequence of our condition: distance.

ITO acts as a means of healing through logotherapy. We, the participants, are the beneficiaries of this therapy, and the assembly of hierarchs, together with the priests and volunteers, are the ones who administer it. In this respect, we identify with the comparison Saint Paul makes in the First Epistle to the Corinthians: “Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually” (1 Cor. 12, 27). Indeed, Saint Paul’s metaphor fits wonderfully with what took place at this ITO, and not only there, since only those who love one another and share the same faith can form a living Eucharistic Chalice.

Year after year I am impressed by the effort of each host Archdiocese. For me, the liturgical experience at Maglavit Monastery moved my heart the most, because it reminded me of the summer liturgies celebrated at my parish in Georgia, USA, in the shade of the oak trees and in the peace of Christ.

Ryan Petru Botaș,
Representative of the Romanian Orthodox Archdiocese of the United States of America at ITO

title: Archdeacon Adrian Sorin Mihalache Met with ROYA Youth in Rochester, NY
intro:
On Saturday, September 7, 2019, a meeting with Archdeacon Adrian Sorin Mihalache, a faculty member of the Faculty of Orthodox Theology in Iași, was organized by ROYA together with Holy Trinity Parish in Rochester, NY. Fr. Sorin led a workshop on developing attention, attended by young people from Toronto and New York together with parishioners of Holy Trinity Parish. In addition to the workshop, Fr. Sorin gave a lecture entitled “The Jamming Signals of the World and Inner Fragmentation”.

The workshop began at 8 in the morning. The participants learned about research on attention in psychology and in theology. What stayed with me was Father’s explanation that in anything we do, intention counts for only ⅛, while 4/8 is the spirit in which we do it. Fr. Sorin used examples from the Holy Fathers along with examples from everyday life, such as structuring the day’s schedule so that it includes both intellectual and physical effort. Besides Father’s presentations, those present took part in various group activities that demanded their attention in a special way. At 12 o’clock we had lunch. Many of us had the chance to speak with Fr. Sorin privately.

The lecture “The Jamming Signals of the World and Inner Fragmentation” followed. At the end, those present were able to ask the speaker questions. The lecture can be found on the ROYA Facebook page. The host, Fr. Daniel Ene, thanked the presenter for the effort and love with which he organized his lecture tour in the United States and gave him an icon of Saint John Maximovitch of San Francisco.

After the lecture, the workshop participants gathered again with Archdeacon Sorin for the second part of the workshop. Father explained that the structure of modern society harms people’s capacity for attention through multiplying demands, entertainment and “multitasking”. Through practical examples, he showed that strengthening the factors that matter in pursuing a goal and reducing the factors that do not matter are necessary in order to reach it. Each participant’s different kind of attention was tested by watching a film.

At the end, the participants shared their personal conclusions. Everyone agreed that the workshop had far exceeded their expectations. For me, this workshop was a great challenge to change my way of thinking. I really liked the way Father showed the connection between psychological research and what the Holy Fathers say. The medical cases of OCD patients healed through a single change in thinking impressed me. Fr. Sorin was a ray of optimism for me. Indeed, I understood that any negative influence can be changed if you give it enough attention. Every participant shared the same sense of optimism instilled by Fr. Sorin. Before leaving for New York City to visit the parishes of our Metropolia, Archdeacon Sorin thanked Fr. Daniel Ene and all those present.

Pompiliu Gârlonța

title: 95th Anniversary of St. Stephen’s Parish, South St. Paul, MN
intro:
On Sunday, September 29, 2019, St. Stephen’s Parish in South St. Paul, MN celebrated the 95th anniversary of its founding. His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae was among the faithful of the parish on this occasion.

The celebration began on Saturday, September 28, with Vespers. After the service, His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae met with the members of the Parish Council to discuss the situation of the parish and the appropriate preparations for the parish’s 100th anniversary.

On Sunday morning the faithful of the parish gathered for the Divine Liturgy celebrated by His Eminence Nicolae and the parish priest, Fr. Ioan Poptelecan. At the appointed time, His Eminence Nicolae explained the Gospel of the day on loving one’s enemies and doing good. The Savior’s words are foolishness to the world we live in, but Christ warned us that we are not of this world. Metropolitan Nicolae recalled the words of Saint Silouan the Athonite, who urges us first to pray for those we consider our enemies, and the peace of Christ will warm our hearts; then to strive to love them, and His grace will help us accomplish what seems humanly impossible. His Eminence Nicolae then spoke about the life of the Venerable Irodion of Lainici, whose holy relics and icon had been brought for veneration from SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago. At the end of the homily, His Eminence Nicolae presented the parish with a new antimension and urged the parish priest, Fr. Ioan Poptelecan, and the faithful to use this anniversary to examine the parish’s plans for the future, especially those concerning community programs for children, youth and adults.

A festive meal followed, with traditional Romanian dishes enjoyed by many American friends of the parish. John Omorean livened up the program with the three folk dance groups he trains: Dunărea, made up of children, Plai de dor, made up of young women, and Izvorașul, to the delight of the audience. Mr. Patrick Ledray, Honorary Consul of Romania in Minneapolis, attended the event.

title: Deanery Assembly for the Central US at Saint John Cassian Parish, San Antonio, Texas
intro:
Every two years, the priests and delegates of each parish of the Romanian Orthodox Archdiocese of the United States of America meet at the Deanery Assembly to present and discuss the situation of the parishes and their pastoral and missionary concerns. At the 2017 Assembly in Troy, MI, it was decided that Saint John Cassian Parish in San Antonio, TX would host this meeting in 2019.

The proceedings of the Assembly began on Friday afternoon, November 1, 2019, with a prayer of blessing offered by His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae. This was followed by the roll call, the presentation of the Agenda, and the reading and approval of the minutes of the previous Assembly of November 2017. Our host, Fr. Valentin Ilieș, welcomed us and showed us the rented space the parish used for more than 2 years, as well as the new church that was purchased, reinforced and adapted to the requirements of the Orthodox tradition. The guest of honor at the meeting was Hieromonk Petru Pruteanu, author of important liturgical works and a friend of the parish.

The first topic on the Assembly’s Agenda was dedicated to the 90th anniversary of the founding of the Romanian Missionary Episcopate in America, followed by a presentation on the Commemorative Year of Patriarchs Nicodim Munteanu and Iustin Moisescu and of the translators of church books in the Romanian Patriarchate. The session continued with the presentation of the projects completed and the problems encountered in each parish of the Deanery over the last two years. Friday ended with a meeting of His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae with the priests of the Deanery, at which several pastoral and catechetical projects to be implemented in the coming period were discussed.

The work of the Assembly resumed the next day, Saturday, November 2, with the presentation of the topic “From the Life of the Romanian Village” by Fr. Aurel Sas of St. Simeon Parish in Detroit, MI. The presentation was accompanied by a viewing of the exhibition “Chipul satului românesc”, received from the Romanian Patriarchate with the blessing of His Beatitude Patriarch Daniel. Fr. Iulian Aniței of Protection of the Mother of God Parish in Houston, TX continued, complementing the presentation dedicated to the Commemorative Year with a presentation of the efforts of church translators, from the first appearances in the Romanian language up to those of our own times. Fr. Iulian mentioned the pastoral and missionary need for a work of translating Romanian theologians and fathers into English.

The next part of the Assembly was dedicated to the reports on the various activities in the parishes. The report of the Ladies’ Association (AROLA) was read by Mrs. Mirela Manga of Holy Trinity Parish in Troy, MI, a member of the AROLA committee; the report on the activities of the Sunday School was prepared and read by Mrs. Violeta Vancea, coordinator of the School at SS. Constantine and Helen Cathedral in Chicago; and the report of ROYA (the Youth Association) by Macrina Aniței, Alexandru and Andrei Barbolovici. The election of the Deanery Consistory was the last item on the Agenda of this meeting.

His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae expressed his thanks to Dean Fr. Călin Barbolovici, to Fr. Valentin Ilieș and to all the faithful of the parish for the beautiful organization of this Deanery Assembly. Since it was the Saturday of the Departed, a memorial service for those who have fallen asleep followed. The day ended with His Eminence Metropolitan Nicolae and the priests present attending the Vespers service at St. Anthony the Great Church (OCA) in San Antonio, where Fr. Prof. John Behr of St. Vladimir’s Orthodox Theological Seminary in New York gave a lecture.

Recorded by Gabriel Ilieș, secretary of the Assembly
